# Modular Planters: design

Date: 2026-10-28. Status: approved by the owner on 2026-10-28.

Modular Planters is an addon for Agritech: Evolved (ATE). It lets a player replace dozens or hundreds of ATE Advanced Planters with a few multiblocks, while each one produces, draws and costs about what the same number of Advanced Planters would.

Choices marked **(my call)** were made by Claude, the assistant writing this, and haven't been confirmed by the owner yet. Everything else was decided by the owner. The brainstorm record, with the research behind these numbers, is `NOTES.md` in the mod folder.

## Why

The owner's farm runs about 400 ATE Advanced Planters, mostly Mystical Agriculture seeds. 333 of them grow nickel for a reactor fuel line, each with 2 Speed Upgrade MK3s, insanium farmland and a cloche. Those nickel seeds are maxed in every Productive Farming trait (see "Seed traits"). Every planter needs its own seed, soil, two upgrades and a Logistics Networks (LN) node on three channels: energy in, fertilizer in, outputs out. Adding capacity means placing and configuring one more planter and one more node each time.

The mod collapses this into a few multiblocks. A planter block holding 64 seeds stands in for 64 Advanced Planters. One connection to the multiblock's core replaces the per-planter nodes.

## Goals

- A planter block with N growing seeds produces what N Advanced Planters with the same seed, soil, upgrades and fertilizer produce, and draws the same power.
- A fully upgraded planter block costs about what 64 upgraded Advanced Planters cost.
- One connection to the core (an LN node, a cable, pipes, or the ME block) runs a whole multiblock.
- Planter blocks that can't be reached in a build can still be managed from the core's screen.
- It works in any modpack: it follows the pack's ATE config and recipes, and its own recipes are datapack recipes a pack can replace.

## Non-goals

- No new crops, soils, fertilizers or upgrade items. The mod uses ATE's own Speed and Yield Upgrades and ATE's own planter recipes.
- No dedicated Logistics Networks block. An ordinary LN node on the core does the job.
- NeoForge on Minecraft 26.1.2 only. No Fabric and no other Minecraft versions.
- No 3D scenes in the guide. Oracle Index doesn't support them, so example builds are still images.

## Anti-goals

These would make the mod a failure even if it worked:

- A planter block out-producing the matching number of Advanced Planters, apart from the built-in cloche's yield rule below.
- Voiding items. When there's nowhere to put outputs, planter blocks wait.
- Requiring AE2, Applied Flux or Logistics Networks. All three are optional.
- Hard-coding ATE's default numbers. In game, every ATE number is read from ATE's live config.
- Copying code from ModularBees. ModularBees is LGPL-3.0 and this mod is MIT, so ModularBees may be read for ideas only.

## Constraints

- **Platform:** NeoForge, Minecraft 26.1.2. It must run in the FTB Evolution 2 instance (pack 1.5.1, NeoForge 26.1.2.121) at `~/.ftba/instances/ftb evolution 2`.
- **Dependencies:**
  - Hard: ATE (tested with 2.2.0.6).
  - Optional: AE2 (26.1.13-beta), Applied Flux (26.1-1.0.2), Logistics Networks (26.1.2-1.13.0), Oracle Index (2.0.0), Jade.
  - The mod has to load and work with any combination of the optional ones missing.
- **Identity:**
  - Mod name: Modular Planters.
  - Mod id: `modular_planters`.
  - Java package: `io.github.julianperge.modular_planters`.
  - GitHub repo: `julian-perge/ModularPlanters`.
  - Local folder: `~/DEV/git_repos/minecraft-mods/ModularPlanters`, renamed from `ate-planter-multiblock` (my call).
- **License:** MIT, with every line of code written for this mod. Textures are adapted from ATE's, which are MIT, so ATE's copyright notice ships with the mod.
- **ATE config:** every ATE number is read through ATE's public static getters in `com.misterd.agritechevolved.Config`, for example `Config.getPlanterBasePowerConsumption()`, the same way the Advanced Planter reads them. ATE's defaults appear in this document only as worked examples. Tests may pin those defaults.
- **Logistics Networks tags:** no block in this mod may be in LN's blacklist tags (`logisticsnetwork:blacklist/block` and the item, fluid and chemical variants).

## The blocks

| Block | Job |
|---|---|
| Core | Forms the multiblock, applies the built-in cloche, opens the core screen, and acts as a doorway for energy, fertilizer and outputs. Stores nothing itself. |
| Power | Stores energy. The only place energy is kept. |
| Fertilizer | Stores fertilizer, shared by every planter block. |
| Export | Holds outputs until something pulls them out. |
| Planter | Grows one seed type, up to 64 seeds. |
| ME | Optional, and only exists when AE2 is installed. Connects the multiblock to an AE2 network. |
| Frame | Does nothing except connect parts. |

There's no import block. The fertilizer block covers that job.

### Core

- **It's a doorway.** While formed, the core exposes three capabilities:
  - **Energy:** energy inserted into the core goes to the power blocks.
  - **Fertilizer in:** items inserted into the core go to the fertilizer blocks. Only fertilizers are accepted.
  - **Outputs:** items extracted from the core come out of the export blocks.
  - So one LN node on the core with the owner's existing three-channel settings runs a whole multiblock. Each part block also exposes its own resource directly, so cables and pipes can connect to the power, fertilizer or export blocks instead.
- **While not formed**, the core exposes no capabilities (my call).
- **It applies the built-in cloche to every planter block.** The cloche is always on and needs no item. See "Built-in cloche".
- **Its screen** is described under "Core screen".

### Power block

- Stores energy. Several power blocks pool their storage (my call).
- Buffer: 4,000,000 RF each, the same as ATE's Capacitor Tier 3, which is its key recipe ingredient (my call). This is set in the mod's server config.
- Accepts energy at least as fast as the whole multiblock can draw it, with no low per-tick limit (my call). ATE's Tier 3 Capacitor moves only 8,192 RF/t, which wouldn't cover even one full planter block.
- Energy can't be extracted from it (my call).
- When broken, it keeps its stored energy in the dropped item, like ATE's capacitors (my call).

### Fertilizer block

- 27 slots (my call). Accepts only items in ATE's `agritechevolved:fertilizers` data map.
- Several fertilizer blocks pool their contents (my call).
- Drops its contents when broken.

### Export block

- 54 slots (my call). Only the multiblock can insert. Anything can extract.
- Several export blocks fill one after another (my call).
- Drops its contents when broken.

### Planter block

The planter block's own behavior is described under "How a planter block grows".

### ME block

- Only exists when AE2 is installed: the block's registration, item and recipe are all conditional on AE2.
- It's an AE2 grid node that uses one channel. A multiblock can have at most one. A second ME block keeps the multiblock from forming, since it would do nothing (my call).
- **Outputs:**
  - Harvested outputs go straight into ME storage.
  - Whatever ME doesn't accept goes into the export blocks.
  - Every 20 ticks, the ME block also moves whatever is in the export blocks into ME (my call).
- **Fertilizer:**
  - The ME block's screen has one filter slot where the player picks a fertilizer.
  - Every 20 ticks, the ME block tops the fertilizer blocks up with that fertilizer from ME (my call).
- **Applied Flux:**
  - When Applied Flux is also installed, the ME block keeps the power blocks charged from the network's stored FE.
  - Each tick, before the planter blocks run, it fills the power blocks' free room from the network's FE, so they stay full and their bars show stored power. Filling empty power blocks takes up to their capacity, 4,000,000 RF each, out of the network once (owner ruling, 2026-10-30, after in-game testing: the earlier rule drew only what the planter blocks asked for the tick before, so the power blocks always showed 0 and looked broken).
  - Without Applied Flux, power comes in through the core or the power blocks.
  - A Flux Accessor placed against the core or a power block also works either way, with no code in this mod.

### Frame block

- Connects parts and does nothing else.
- It's also the in-between step when crafting a planter block (see "Recipes").

## Structure

- **Free form.** The multiblock is the core plus every part block connected to it face to face, directly or through other parts. Diagonal contact doesn't connect.
- **Size cap:** at most 24 parts, not counting the core. Frames count (my call).
  - Above the cap, the multiblock doesn't form, and the core's screen says why.
  - The cap is in the server config, default 24 (my call).
- **Required parts:** at least one power block, one export block and one planter block. Fertilizer, ME and frame blocks are optional.
- **Two cores:** if the connected parts reach a second core, neither forms. The core's screen names the problem block and its position (my call).
- **Re-checking:** the core re-checks the shape when a part next to the structure is placed or broken.
- **When the shape breaks:** the planter blocks stop, but every block keeps its contents.

The guide shows three example builds from the brainstorm, saved in `mockups/layouts.html`. They're examples only, since any connected shape works:

- **Raised bed under a cloche:** corner legs, a 3x3 bed and a 3x3 glass canopy.
- **Vertical farm:** a 2x2 tower with the core on the bottom floor and floors of planter blocks above it.
- **Rosette:** one block tall. The core is in the center, the other parts take the four diagonal corners, and planter blocks extend outward in four arms.

## How a planter block grows

### Contents

The planter block's screen has four slots, all filled by hand. They can also be filled from the core's screen.

| Slot | Holds |
|---|---|
| Seed | A seed bin: up to 64 seeds of one item type. Anything a Advanced Planter accepts, saplings included. See "Seed traits". |
| Soil | One soil type, up to 64. Anything in ATE's `agritechevolved:soil_modifiers` data map, including Mystical Agradditions cruxes. |
| Upgrade 1 | One ATE upgrade type (Speed or Yield, MK1 to MK3), up to 64. |
| Upgrade 2 | Same as upgrade 1. |

- There's no fertilizer slot and there are no output slots. Fertilizer comes from the fertilizer blocks, and outputs go to the export blocks or ME.

### Seed traits

Other mods can change a seed through ATE's planter events. Productive Farming, which FTB Evolution 2 includes, gives seeds traits such as Growth and Yield. Each harvest can raise one trait, and ATE writes the changed seed back into the planter. Seeds whose traits differ don't stack. The owner chose that every seed in a planter block keeps its own traits, so a planter block matches the same number of Advanced Planters exactly:

- **What the bin holds:** up to 64 seeds of one item type, each kept as its own stack of 1 with its own data. Seeds of the same item with different traits can go in together. Players moving from Advanced Planters can put in all their seeds without sorting them.
- **How the slot looks:** on screen the bin looks like one slot showing the seed and the count. Hovering over it lists how many seeds have each trait combination (my call).
- **Bin order:** seeds stay in the order they were put in (my call). The seed numbering below follows that order.
- **Taking seeds out:** the builder decides how seeds are taken back out of the bin.
- **Each seed levels on its own,** exactly as it would in its own Advanced Planter.
- **No Productive Farming code:** all of this works through ATE's events, so Productive Farming isn't a dependency.
- The seed and soil must be a valid pair under ATE's planter recipes (`agritechevolved:crop` and `agritechevolved:tree`). The mod reads those recipes, so new ATE crops and KubeJS recipes work without changes.

### Seeds, soil and upgrades

- **Growing seeds:** G = the smaller of the seed count and the soil count. 64 seeds on 13 soil grow the first 13 in bin order. The other 51 are idle, and the screen says so.
- **One upgrade covers one seed.** Let A = the smaller of upgrade 1's count and G, and B = the smaller of upgrade 2's count and G. Number the growing seeds 1 to G. Seed i gets upgrade 1 if i is at most A, and upgrade 2 if i is at most B. So by upgrades the seeds fall into at most three sets:
  - The smaller of A and B: seeds with both upgrades.
  - The larger minus the smaller: seeds with only the fuller slot's upgrade.
  - G minus the larger: seeds with no upgrade.
- **Groups:** a group is a set of growing seeds with the same upgrade set and identical seed data, traits included. Seeds with different traits are in different groups even when they have the same upgrades.
- **Why seeds pair up this way (my call):** it matches a player filling Advanced Planters one at a time with both upgrades before starting the next.
- **The screen shows coverage:** "23/64 seeds upgraded" when upgrades run short, and "13 working, 51 idle" when soil runs short.

### Growth

Each group behaves exactly like that many Advanced Planters with that upgrade set, running in lockstep:

- **Progress:** each group keeps its own progress counter.
- **Growth time:** recomputed every tick with ATE's formula: `max(1, round(advanced base processing time / (soil x upgrade speed x fertilizer speed x cloche speed)))`.
  - Upgrade speed uses ATE's Speed Upgrade multipliers and Yield Upgrade speed penalties, as in `AdvancedPlanterBlockEntity.getModuleSpeedModifier`.
  - Cloche speed is ATE's configured cloche speed bonus.
  - The planter block then fires ATE's `PlanterProcessingTimeEvent` once for the group, passing itself as the planter and one of the group's seeds. Every seed in a group has identical data, so one event speaks for all of them. The planter block uses whatever time the event returns. That's how Productive Farming's Growth trait applies.
- **Harvest:** when a group's progress reaches its growth time, the whole group harvests at once.
- **After a harvest,** seeds whose traits just changed form new groups. Every seed that harvested starts again at zero, so no progress is lost or gained.

### Power

- **Draw per tick:** for each group still growing, the number of seeds times `round(base power consumption x upgrade power multiplier)`. Only Speed Upgrades raise power, as in ATE's `getModulePowerModifier`.
- **When there isn't enough:** if the power blocks can't cover the planter block's full draw for a tick, no group in that planter block advances that tick. A planter block never runs only some of its seeds.
- **Who gets power first (my call):** planter blocks draw in a fixed order, sorted by block position. When power runs short, the same planter blocks keep running and the rest pause, so it doesn't flicker between them.
- **Waiting to harvest:** a group that's ready to harvest but waiting for output room draws no power, as in ATE.

### Fertilizer

Each growing seed uses fertilizer at ATE's rate, one item per harvest, so N seeds use what N Advanced Planters would.

- **Which fertilizer (my call):** the fertilizer used is the item in the first non-empty slot of the fertilizer blocks, taken in a fixed order.
- **When a group counts as fertilized (my call, revised 2026-10-29 after the final review):** each tick, the fertilizer stored is a budget shared by every planter block of the core. Planter blocks claim from it in the same position order as power, and each group claims as many items as it has seeds, all or nothing. A group that claims is fertilized for that tick. A group that can't claim runs unfertilized that tick, so one stack can't speed up more seeds than it could pay for. A fertilized group uses the fertilizer's speed and yield multipliers from ATE's `agritechevolved:fertilizers` data map, and consumes one item per seed when it harvests. Otherwise the group runs unfertilized.
- **No fertilizer block:** if there's no fertilizer block, or it's empty, every planter block runs unfertilized.

### Harvest and outputs

When a group harvests, each seed in it goes through the same steps, in the same order as ATE's Advanced Planter (`AdvancedPlanterBlockEntity`, around line 584):

1. Fire `PlanterPreHarvestEvent` for that seed, passing the planter block as the planter. Write the seed the event returns back into that seed's place in the bin. This is where Productive Farming raises a trait.
2. Roll that seed's drops from ATE's recipe, including chance drops, using the seed the event returned.
3. Apply ATE's yield rounding to each drop. This is r in "Built-in cloche".
4. Fire `PlanterPostHarvestEvent` for that seed with its own drop list. Productive Farming adds its Yield bonus to each stack in that list, so each seed must get its own event and its own list.
5. Add the cloche's kept fraction for each drop to the planter block's remainders. Extra items from the remainders are added after the event, never into the event's list, so per-stack bonuses from other mods never apply to them.
6. Insert the drops into ME, if there's an online ME block, and then into the export blocks.
7. Consume one fertilizer for that seed, if the group is fertilized.

Output room (my call):

- A group only starts harvesting if the export blocks, plus ME if it's online, have room for the group's drops as ATE's recipe lists them. This is like ATE's `hasOutputSpace`.
- Other mods can add to the drops during the events, so they may still not all fit. Whatever doesn't fit is held inside the planter block, and the planter block pauses until all of it has been moved out.
- Nothing is voided.

### Built-in cloche

The built-in cloche is always on and uses ATE's configured cloche speed and yield bonuses. They're 1.15 and 1.10 by default.

**Speed:** the cloche speed bonus goes into the growth time formula above.

**Yield:** ATE's Advanced Planter gives `max(1, round(count x fertilizer yield x upgrade yield x cloche yield))` for each drop. For a 1-item drop at 1.1 that rounds back to 1, so the cloche's yield bonus does nothing for Mystical Agriculture essence. The built-in cloche keeps the fraction that rounding throws away. The owner decided this; it's the mod's one deliberate buff.

The exact rule (my call, written so that it never gives less than ATE and never adds more than the cloche's own share):

1. For each drop, let x = count x fertilizer yield x upgrade yield, and e = x x cloche yield.
2. ATE's result is r = max(1, round(e)). The player always gets at least r.
3. The fraction kept is the smaller of (e - r) and x x (cloche yield - 1), or 0 if e - r is negative.
4. Add the kept fraction to a running remainder for that item, saved per planter block. Each time the remainder reaches 1, give one extra item and subtract 1.

The yield bonus from other mods, such as Productive Farming's Yield trait, is added after this rule and never counts toward x or e.

With the default 1.1 and a 1-item drop, each seed gets one extra every tenth harvest, a 10% gain. With a Yield MK3 (2.0), e is 2.2 and r is 2, so the cloche adds 0.2 per drop, again 10%. It also applies to seeds and fertilized essence, the same way ATE's yield bonus does (my call).

### Changing contents mid-growth

The builder decides how progress is kept when a player changes seeds, soil or upgrades mid-growth. The rule is that no change can produce a harvest earlier or larger than the same change to Advanced Planters would. Changing the seed or soil type resets progress, as in ATE.

## Core screen

The owner approved the layout in `mockups/core-screen.html`. It's modeled on the Logistics Networks Computer's Node Table (`LogisticsNetworks/src/main/resources/assets/logisticsnetworks/guides/logisticsnetworks/guide/computer/node-table.md`).

- **Top bar:**
  - Formed state and part count, for example "FORMED 18 / 24".
  - When the multiblock isn't formed, the reason, naming the problem block and its position if there is one.
- **Totals:** stored power and current draw, fertilizer stored, how full the export blocks are, and ME status.
- **Planter table:**
  - One row per planter block, grouped by seed type under collapsible headings, the way LN groups nodes by label.
  - Each row shows:
    - the seed;
    - how many seeds are growing;
    - upgrade coverage;
    - a status: growing, short on soil, paused for power, paused for a full export, or idle;
    - the block's position.
- **Row buttons:**
  - **Outline** toggles a glowing outline on that planter block in the world, visible only to that player, like LN's lamp button.
  - **Open** opens that planter block's screen remotely. It's the same screen as in the world, with a "Back to core" button added.
- **Rules:**
  - The table updates live.
  - Opening a planter block remotely is checked on the server: the player must be in range of the core, and the planter block must belong to that core's formed multiblock.

## Integrations

### Logistics Networks

- There's no LN code in the mod. A node on the core works through the core's doorway capabilities.
- The node needs an upgrade sized to the multiblock. A node uses its best upgrade for every channel, and LN's default limits are:

| Node upgrade | Energy per tick | Items a second |
|---|---|---|
| None | 2,000 RF | 0.8 |
| Iron | 10,000 RF | 64 |
| Gold | 50,000 RF | 256 |
| Diamond | 250,000 RF | 5,120 |
| Netherite | about 2.1 billion RF | 200,000 |

- Example with ATE's defaults: a full planter block of 64 nickel seeds with 2 Speed Upgrade MK3s, insanium farmland and the built-in cloche.
  - **Power:** it draws 32,768 RF/t whatever the seeds' traits.
  - **Items:** with seeds that have no traits, it puts out about 24 items a second. With seeds maxed in Productive Farming's Growth and Yield, like the owner's, it puts out about 320 items a second. That's more than a gold upgrade moves.
  - **Upgrade needed:** a diamond upgrade covers up to 7 such planter blocks, and power is the limit. More than 7 needs a netherite upgrade, or more nodes on the power blocks.
- The guide has to include this table and example.

### AE2 and Applied Flux

See the ME block above. AE2 and Applied Flux are compile-time-only dependencies. All code that touches them sits behind a mod-loaded check, so the mod loads without them.

### Productive Farming

- There's no Productive Farming code in the mod. Its traits work through ATE's three planter events, fired as described under "How a planter block grows".
- It's in FTB Evolution 2, with `statsOnExternalCrops = true`, so Mystical Agriculture seeds gain traits there. Manual testing uses that pack.

### Jade

An optional Jade plugin (my call, the lowest priority in the mod):

- On the core: formed state.
- On a planter block: growing seeds and status.

### JEI

No JEI plugin. The crafting recipes show up in JEI on their own, and the crops are ATE's own planter recipes, which ATE already shows.

## Recipes

These are shaped crafting recipes, shipped as datapack JSON so packs can replace them. The owner chose each key ingredient. The other ingredients and the grid patterns are my calls.

| Block | Pattern | Key |
|---|---|---|
| Frame | `PPP` `PIP` `PPP` | P = ATE Advanced Planter (`agritechevolved:advanced_planter`), I = block of iron |
| Planter | `FFF` `FIF` `FFF` | F = Frame, I = ATE Infused Farmland (`agritechevolved:infused_farmland`) |
| Core | `IGI` `GCG` `IDI` | C = ATE Cloche Dome (`agritechevolved:cloche_dome`), G = glass (`#c:glass_blocks`), I = block of iron, D = block of diamond |
| Power | `IRI` `RCR` `IRI` | C = ATE Capacitor Tier 3 (`agritechevolved:capacitor_tier3`), R = block of redstone, I = block of iron |
| Fertilizer | `IBI` `BSB` `IBI` | S = ATE Fertilizer Spreader (`agritechevolved:fertilizer_spreader`), B = bone block, I = block of iron |
| Export | `IHI` `HSH` `IHI` | S = ATE Silo (`agritechevolved:silo`), H = hopper, I = block of iron |
| ME | `IFI` `FXF` `IFI` | X = ME Interface (`#ae2:interface`), F = fluix crystal (`#c:gems/fluix`), I = block of iron. Has a `neoforge:mod_loaded` condition on `ae2`. |

The owner's reasoning:

- **Progression:** a player builds their first Modular Planter in the mid to late game, when they already farm diamonds, emeralds and netherite.
- **Gating:** the power block carries the progression gate. Every multiblock needs one, and a Tier 3 Capacitor takes diamonds and emeralds.
- **Two-step planter block:** it takes 64 Advanced Planters, and splitting that into two steps keeps any one recipe from needing stacks of an item.
- **Following the pack:** using Advanced Planters means a pack that makes them cost more makes planter blocks cost more too. Players can also break existing Advanced Planters and craft them straight in.
- **Iron for the frame:** a frame used as filler costs 8 Advanced Planters, and an iron center keeps it from also costing 9 diamonds.
- **No frames in the other parts:** they aren't crafted from frames, which would add 8 Advanced Planters to each.

## Textures and models

- Every block is a full cube (my call).
- Textures are adapted from ATE's, in `AgritechEvolved/src/main/resources/assets/agritechevolved/textures/block/`, so the blocks look like part of ATE. For example:
  - the power block from the capacitor textures;
  - the core from the cloche dome textures;
  - the planter block from the planter textures.
- Planter blocks don't render their crops (my call). A planter block can switch between an "on" and an "off" texture while growing, the way ATE's capacitors do (my call).

## Server config

The mod's own server config holds (my call):

- the part cap (default 24);
- the power block's buffer (default 4,000,000 RF);
- the ME block's export and fertilizer interval (default 20 ticks).

ATE's numbers are never copied into this config. They're always read from ATE.

## Guide

The guide is an Oracle Index book, set up the way Oritech does it:

- The pages live in a `wiki/` folder, using the moddedmc.wiki layout.
- `processResources` copies them into `assets/oracle_index/books/modular_planters`.
- Oracle Index is `compileOnly`, so it isn't needed at runtime.

Pages:

- An overview.
- One page per block, with its recipe.
- The building rules.
- The three example builds as still images.
- The planter block's seed, soil and upgrade rules.
- The built-in cloche rule.
- The Logistics Networks upgrade table and example.
- AE2 and Applied Flux.

The Oritech repo at `~/DEV/git_repos/minecraft-mods/Oritech` is the working example to copy the setup from.

## Testing

- **Unit tests** for the math:
  - grouping seeds by upgrade coverage;
  - the soil limit;
  - growth time and power draw per group;
  - fertilizer use;
  - the cloche yield rule.
  - One test checks that a planter block with N seeds gives the same expected output and power as N simulated Advanced Planters, using ATE's default numbers.
  - One test registers a listener on ATE's three events that acts like Productive Farming: it changes the seed and adds a flat bonus to each drop stack. The test checks that seeds level on their own, that each seed gets its own post-harvest event, and that the cloche's extra items never get the bonus.
- **NeoForge GameTests** for the world behavior:
  - forming and breaking;
  - the part cap and the two-core case;
  - missing required parts;
  - pausing for power and for full exports;
  - the core's doorway capabilities;
  - contents kept when the shape breaks.
- **Manual play** in the FTB Evolution 2 instance, including a Logistics Networks node on the core and an ME block with Applied Flux.

## Left to the builder

- **Build setup:** the Gradle setup, the NeoForge and Java versions within the constraints above, and the code structure.
- **Multiblock mechanics:** how forming and re-checking are triggered, and how the structure behaves across chunk borders and unloaded chunks. Whatever happens, items must never be lost or duplicated.
- **NeoForge 26.1 APIs:** how the doorway and part capabilities are wired with the transfer API that ATE already uses (`ResourceHandler<ItemResource>`, `ItemStacksResourceHandler`).
- **Screens:** the menu, screen and network code for the core screen and remote opening.
- **AE2 and Applied Flux:** how the ME block uses their APIs. ModularBees' `xmod/ae/` and the Applied Flux jar are references, read but not copied.
- **Changing contents mid-growth:** the exact progress rule, within the rule stated above. Seeds added mid-growth must not join a group's progress.
- **The seed bin:** how players take seeds back out of it.
- **Assets:** how the textures are edited, and how the guide's images are made.

## Calls made without the owner

These are listed together so the owner can check them:

1. Parts:
   - several power blocks and several fertilizer blocks pool their contents, and several export blocks fill one after another;
   - the power block buffer is 4,000,000 RF, the fertilizer block has 27 slots, and the export block has 54.
2. Energy:
   - the power block accepts energy as fast as the multiblock can use it;
   - energy can't be extracted from it;
   - it keeps its energy when broken.
3. Structure rules:
   - the core exposes nothing while not formed;
   - frames count toward the cap, and the cap is in the server config;
   - a second ME block or a second core stops the multiblock from forming.
4. The ME block:
   - it moves export contents into ME every 20 ticks;
   - it tops fertilizer up every 20 ticks from one chosen fertilizer;
   - with Applied Flux, it keeps the power blocks full from the network's FE.
5. Upgrade coverage pairs both upgrades on the same seeds first.
6. Power: planter blocks are powered in a fixed order by position.
7. Fertilizer:
   - the first fertilizer found in the fertilizer blocks is the one used;
   - a group counts as fertilized only when there's enough for all its seeds.
8. Seed bin:
   - seeds keep the order they were put in;
   - hovering over the bin lists the trait combinations.
9. The exact cloche yield rule, applying it to every drop, and adding its extras after the post-harvest event.
10. Output room: a group starts harvesting when there's room for its listed drops, and anything other mods add that doesn't fit is held in the planter block until it's moved out.
11. Recipes: every ingredient and pattern other than the key ingredients.
12. Looks:
    - full cube blocks with no crop rendering;
    - an on and off texture for the planter block.
13. An optional Jade plugin, and no JEI plugin.
14. The server config contents.
15. The local folder `~/DEV/git_repos/minecraft-mods/ModularPlanters`.

# GLOSSARY.md Format

## Structure

```md
# {Context Name}

{One or two sentence description of what this context is and why it exists.}

## Language

**Order**:
{A one or two sentence description of the term}
_Avoid_: Purchase, transaction

**Invoice**:
A request for payment sent to a customer after delivery.
_Avoid_: Bill, payment request

**Customer**:
A person or organization that places orders.
_Avoid_: Client, buyer, account
```

## Rules

- **Be opinionated.** When multiple words exist for the same concept, pick the best one and list the others under `_Avoid_`.
- **Keep definitions tight.** One or two sentences max. Define what it IS, not what it does.
- **Only include terms specific to this project's context.** General programming concepts (timeouts, error types, utility patterns) don't belong even if the project uses them extensively. Before adding a term, ask: is this a concept unique to this context, or a general programming concept? Only the former belongs.
- **Group terms under subheadings** when natural clusters emerge. If all terms belong to a single cohesive area, a flat list is fine.

## Single vs multi-context repos

**Single context (most repos):** One `GLOSSARY.md` at the repo root.

**Multiple contexts:** A `GLOSSARY-MAP.md` at the repo root lists the contexts, where they live, and how they relate to each other:

```md
# Glossary Map

## Contexts

- [Ordering](./src/ordering/GLOSSARY.md): receives and tracks customer orders
- [Billing](./src/billing/GLOSSARY.md): generates invoices and processes payments
- [Fulfillment](./src/fulfillment/GLOSSARY.md): manages warehouse picking and shipping

## Relationships

- **Ordering → Fulfillment**: Ordering emits `OrderPlaced` events; Fulfillment consumes them to start picking
- **Fulfillment → Billing**: Fulfillment emits `ShipmentDispatched` events; Billing consumes them to generate invoices
- **Ordering ↔ Billing**: Shared types for `CustomerId` and `Money`
```

The skill infers which structure applies:

- If `GLOSSARY-MAP.md` exists, read it to find contexts
- If only a root `GLOSSARY.md` exists, single context
- If neither exists, create a root `GLOSSARY.md` lazily when the first term is resolved

When multiple contexts exist, infer which one the current topic relates to. If unclear, ask.
=====ADR
# ADR Format

ADRs live in `docs/adr/` and use sequential numbering: `0001-slug.md`, `0002-slug.md`, etc.

Create the `docs/adr/` directory lazily: only when the first ADR is needed.

## Template

```md
# {Short title of the decision}

{1-3 sentences: what's the context, what did we decide, and why.}
```

That's it. An ADR can be a single paragraph. The value is in recording *that* a decision was made and *why*, not in filling out sections.

## Optional sections

Only include these when they add genuine value. Most ADRs won't need them.

- **Status** frontmatter (`proposed | accepted | deprecated | superseded by ADR-NNNN`): useful when decisions are revisited
- **Considered Options**: only when the rejected alternatives are worth remembering
- **Consequences**: only when non-obvious downstream effects need to be called out

## Numbering

Scan `docs/adr/` for the highest existing number and increment by one.

## When to offer an ADR

All three of these must be true:

1. **Hard to reverse**: the cost of changing your mind later is meaningful
2. **Surprising without context**: a future reader will look at the code and wonder "why on earth did they do it this way?"
3. **The result of a real trade-off**: there were genuine alternatives and you picked one for specific reasons

If a decision is easy to reverse, skip it: you'll just reverse it. If it's not surprising, nobody will wonder why. If there was no real alternative, there's nothing to record beyond "we did the obvious thing."

### What qualifies

- **Architectural shape.** "We're using a monorepo." "The write model is event-sourced, the read model is projected into Postgres."
- **Integration patterns between contexts.** "Ordering and Billing communicate via domain events, not synchronous HTTP."
- **Technology choices that carry lock-in.** Database, message bus, auth provider, deployment target. Not every library: just the ones that would take a quarter to swap out.
- **Boundary and scope decisions.** "Customer data is owned by the Customer context; other contexts reference it by ID only." The explicit no-s are as valuable as the yes-s.
- **Deliberate deviations from the obvious path.** "We're using manual SQL instead of an ORM because X." Anything where a reasonable reader would assume the opposite. These stop the next engineer from "fixing" something that was deliberate.
- **Constraints not visible in the code.** "We can't use AWS because of compliance requirements." "Response times must be under 200ms because of the partner API contract."
- **Rejected alternatives when the rejection is non-obvious.** If you considered GraphQL and picked REST for subtle reasons, record it; otherwise someone will suggest GraphQL again in six months.

content.text: Writing `GLOSSARY.md` and the four ADRs.

input.content:
# Modular Planters

An addon for Agritech: Evolved that replaces many Advanced Planters with a few multiblocks. A block of N growing seeds produces, draws power and costs about what N Advanced Planters would.

## Language

### The multiblock

**Multiblock**:
A Modular Planter Core together with every part connected to it face to face, directly or through other parts. Diagonal contact does not connect.
_Avoid_: structure, machine

**Formed**:
A multiblock that meets the building rules and is running. A multiblock that is not formed keeps every block's contents but grows nothing.
_Avoid_: active, assembled

**Problem**:
The reason a multiblock is not formed, such as a second Core, too many parts, or a missing required part.
_Avoid_: error

**Part**:
Any Modular Planter block that joins a multiblock, other than the Core: Power, Fertilizer, Export, Planter, ME or Frame.
_Avoid_: module, component

**Modular Planter Core**:
The block that forms the multiblock, applies the built-in cloche to every Modular Planter Block, and opens the Core screen. It stores nothing itself.
_Avoid_: Planter Core, controller

**Doorway**:
The three resources a formed Core exposes to outside connections: energy in, fertilizer in, and outputs out.
_Avoid_: port, interface

**Modular Planter Power Block**:
Stores the multiblock's energy. Several Power Blocks pool their storage, and energy cannot be extracted from them.
_Avoid_: Planter Power, capacitor

**Modular Planter Fertilizer Block**:
Stores fertilizer for every Modular Planter Block in the multiblock. Several Fertilizer Blocks pool their contents.
_Avoid_: Planter Fertilizer, import block

**Modular Planter Export Block**:
Holds harvested outputs until something pulls them out. Only the multiblock inserts into it.
_Avoid_: Planter Export, output block

**Modular Planter Block**:
Grows one seed type, up to 64 seeds, from one soil type and up to two upgrade types.
_Avoid_: Planter Block, planter

**Modular Planter ME Block**:
An optional Part, present only when AE2 is installed, that connects the multiblock to an AE2 network. A multiblock can have at most one.
_Avoid_: ME interface, Planter ME

**Modular Planter Frame**:
A Part that does nothing except connect other Parts. It counts toward the part cap.
_Avoid_: Planter Frame

### Growing

**Seed**:
Any item an Advanced Planter accepts for planting, saplings included. Each seed carries its own data, such as traits added by other mods.

**Seed bin**:
The Modular Planter Block's seed slot. It holds up to 64 seeds of one item type, each with its own data, in the order they were added.
_Avoid_: seed stack

**Soil**:
The one soil type in a Modular Planter Block, up to 64 items. It limits how many seeds can grow.

**Upgrade**:
An ATE Speed or Yield upgrade item in a Modular Planter Block. One upgrade item covers one seed.
_Avoid_: module (ATE's own names and the `soil_and_modules` save key keep it)

**Growing seed**:
A seed that has soil to grow in. The number of growing seeds is the smaller of the seed count and the soil count. The rest are idle.
_Avoid_: active seed

**Upgrade coverage**:
How many growing seeds each upgrade slot reaches. Both slots cover the same seeds first, in bin order.

**Group**:
A set of growing seeds in one Modular Planter Block with the same upgrade set and identical seed data. A group grows and harvests together, like that many Advanced Planters in lockstep.
_Avoid_: batch, cohort, stack

**Fertilized**:
A group that claimed enough fertilizer for all its seeds that tick. A group that cannot claim runs unfertilized.

**Built-in cloche**:
The cloche effect every Modular Planter Block gets from the Core. It is always on, needs no item, and uses ATE's configured cloche bonuses.
_Avoid_: cloche dome (the Core's recipe ingredient)

**Remainder**:
The fraction of a yield bonus that ATE's rounding would discard. The built-in cloche carries it forward and adds one item each time it reaches a whole one.
_Avoid_: leftover, rounding bonus

**Held output**:
A drop that did not fit in the Export Blocks or ME. The Modular Planter Block pauses until all held outputs have moved out.
_Avoid_: overflow

**Status**:
What a Modular Planter Block is doing: growing, short on soil, paused for power, paused for a full export, or idle.

### Screens

**Core screen**:
The Core's screen. It shows the multiblock's totals and one row per Modular Planter Block, and can open any block's own screen remotely.
_Avoid_: controller screen

**Seed heading**:
A collapsible heading on the Core screen that lists Modular Planter Blocks by seed type.
_Avoid_: group

### Outside the mod

**Agritech: Evolved (ATE)**:
The mod this one extends. It owns the crops, soils, fertilizers, upgrades and the numbers everything is measured against.
_Avoid_: Agritech

**Advanced Planter**:
ATE's planter block, the baseline a Modular Planter Block must match.
_Avoid_: Powered Planter

**Optional mod**:
AE2, Applied Flux, Logistics Networks, Oracle Index or Jade. The mod loads and works with any of them missing.
_Avoid_: soft dependency, addon

**Guide**:
The in-game Oracle Index book that explains the mod.
_Avoid_: wiki, manual

input.content:
# Seeds keep their own traits

Other mods, such as Productive Farming, change a seed through ATE's planter events, and seeds whose data differs do not stack. A seed bin holds each seed as its own item with its own data and groups seeds with identical data, so every seed levels on its own and a Modular Planter Block matches the same number of Advanced Planters exactly.

Players moving from Advanced Planters can put in all their seeds without sorting them, and the seed slot's tooltip lists how many seeds have each trait combination.

input.content:
# The built-in cloche keeps the rounded-away yield

ATE gives `max(1, round(count x fertilizer yield x upgrade yield x cloche yield))` for each drop, so a one-item drop at the default 1.1 cloche bonus rounds back to 1 and the bonus does nothing for single-item drops such as Mystical Agriculture essence. The owner decided the built-in cloche keeps the fraction that rounding throws away and pays one extra item each time it adds up to 1.

This is the mod's one deliberate buff. It never gives less than ATE and never more than the cloche's own share, and the extras are added after the post-harvest event so bonuses from other mods never apply to them.

input.content:
# Power and fertilizer are all-or-nothing, in block position order

If the Power Blocks cannot cover a Modular Planter Block's full draw for a tick, none of its groups advance that tick, so a block never runs only some of its seeds. Fertilizer works the same way per group: each tick the stored fertilizer is one budget shared by the whole multiblock, and a group either claims one item per seed or runs unfertilized, so one stack cannot speed up more seeds than it could pay for.

Blocks claim power and fertilizer in order of block position. When supply runs short, the same blocks keep running and the rest pause, instead of every block flickering on and off.

# Modular Planters

An addon for Agritech: Evolved that replaces many Advanced Planters with a few multiblocks. A block of N growing seeds produces, draws power and costs about what N Advanced Planters would.

## Language

### The multiblock

**Multiblock**:
A Modular Planter Core together with every part connected to it face to face, directly or through other parts. Diagonal contact does not connect.
_Avoid_: structure, machine

**Formed**:
A multiblock that meets the building rules and is running. A multiblock that is not formed keeps every block's contents but grows nothing.
_Avoid_: active, assembled

**Problem**:
The reason a multiblock is not formed, such as a second Core, too many parts, or a missing required part.
_Avoid_: error

**Part**:
Any Modular Planter block that joins a multiblock, other than the Core: Power, Fertilizer, Export, Planter, ME or Frame.
_Avoid_: module, component

**Modular Planter Core**:
The block that forms the multiblock, applies the built-in cloche to every Modular Planter Block, and opens the Core screen. It stores nothing itself.
_Avoid_: Planter Core, controller

**Doorway**:
The three resources a formed Core exposes to outside connections: energy in, fertilizer in, and outputs out.
_Avoid_: port, interface

**Modular Planter Power Block**:
Stores the multiblock's energy. Several Power Blocks pool their storage, and energy cannot be extracted from them.
_Avoid_: Planter Power, capacitor

**Modular Planter Fertilizer Block**:
Stores fertilizer for every Modular Planter Block in the multiblock. Several Fertilizer Blocks pool their contents.
_Avoid_: Planter Fertilizer, import block

**Modular Planter Export Block**:
Holds harvested outputs until something pulls them out. Only the multiblock inserts into it.
_Avoid_: Planter Export, output block

**Modular Planter Block**:
Grows one seed type, up to 64 seeds, from one soil type and up to two upgrade types.
_Avoid_: Planter Block, planter

**Modular Planter ME Block**:
An optional Part, present only when AE2 is installed, that connects the multiblock to an AE2 network. A multiblock can have at most one.
_Avoid_: ME interface, Planter ME

**Modular Planter Frame**:
A Part that does nothing except connect other Parts. It counts toward the part cap.
_Avoid_: Planter Frame

### Growing

**Seed**:
Any item an Advanced Planter accepts for planting, saplings included. Each seed carries its own data, such as traits added by other mods.

**Seed bin**:
The Modular Planter Block's seed slot. It holds up to 64 seeds of one item type, each with its own data, in the order they were added.
_Avoid_: seed stack

**Soil**:
The one soil type in a Modular Planter Block, up to 64 items. It limits how many seeds can grow.

**Upgrade**:
An ATE Speed or Yield upgrade item in a Modular Planter Block. One upgrade item covers one seed.
_Avoid_: module (ATE's own names and the `soil_and_modules` save key keep it)

**Growing seed**:
A seed that has soil to grow in. The number of growing seeds is the smaller of the seed count and the soil count. The rest are idle.
_Avoid_: active seed

**Upgrade coverage**:
How many growing seeds each upgrade slot reaches. Both slots cover the same seeds first, in bin order.

**Group**:
A set of growing seeds in one Modular Planter Block with the same upgrade set and identical seed data. A group grows and harvests together, like that many Advanced Planters in lockstep.
_Avoid_: batch, cohort, stack

**Fertilized**:
A group that claimed enough fertilizer for all its seeds that tick. A group that cannot claim runs unfertilized.

**Built-in cloche**:
The cloche effect every Modular Planter Block gets from the Core. It is always on, needs no item, and uses ATE's configured cloche bonuses.
_Avoid_: cloche dome (the Core's recipe ingredient)

**Remainder**:
The fraction of a yield bonus that ATE's rounding would discard. The built-in cloche carries it forward and adds one item each time it reaches a whole one.
_Avoid_: leftover, rounding bonus

**Held output**:
A drop that did not fit in the Export Blocks or ME. The Modular Planter Block pauses until all held outputs have moved out.
_Avoid_: overflow

**Status**:
What a Modular Planter Block is doing: growing, short on soil, paused for power, paused for a full export, or idle.

### Screens

**Core screen**:
The Core's screen. It shows the multiblock's totals and one row per Modular Planter Block, and can open any block's own screen remotely.
_Avoid_: controller screen

**Seed heading**:
A collapsible heading on the Core screen that lists Modular Planter Blocks by seed type.
_Avoid_: group

### Outside the mod

**Agritech: Evolved (ATE)**:
The mod this one extends. It owns the crops, soils, fertilizers, upgrades and the numbers everything is measured against.
_Avoid_: Agritech

**Advanced Planter**:
ATE's planter block, the baseline a Modular Planter Block must match.
_Avoid_: Powered Planter

**Optional mod**:
AE2, Applied Flux, Logistics Networks, Oracle Index or Jade. The mod loads and works with any of them missing.
_Avoid_: soft dependency, addon

**Guide**:
The in-game Oracle Index book that explains the mod.
_Avoid_: wiki, manual

# The built-in cloche keeps the rounded-away yield

ATE gives `max(1, round(count x fertilizer yield x upgrade yield x cloche yield))` for each drop, so a one-item drop at the default 1.1 cloche bonus rounds back to 1 and the bonus does nothing for single-item drops such as Mystical Agriculture essence. The owner decided the built-in cloche keeps the fraction that rounding throws away and pays one extra item each time it adds up to 1.

This is the mod's one deliberate buff. It never gives less than ATE and never more than the cloche's own share, and the extras are added after the post-harvest event so bonuses from other mods never apply to them.

1	# Modular Planters plan 4: project pages, logo and contributor docs
2	
3	Date: 2026-10-31. Status: approved by the owner on 2026-11-03 ("plan looks good"), with the answers in `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-31-modular-planters-plan-4-todos.md` folded in below.
4	
5	Choices marked **(my call)** were made by Claude, the assistant writing this, and haven't been confirmed by the owner yet. Everything else was decided by the owner during the brainstorm on 2026-10-31. The main design is `2026-10-28-modular-planters-design.md`.
6	
7	## Why
8	
9	The owner wants to create CurseForge and Modrinth projects for Modular Planters. Before that, they need a one-line summary, a logo, and a project description page. Once players have that page and the in-game guide, the README no longer has to be the player manual. The README turns into a front page for people who browse the GitHub repo or open issues, and it is joined by contributor and developer docs.
10	
11	## What a visitor should take away
12	
13	Someone scrolling past the project on CurseForge should see straight away that it is a multiblock addon for Agritech: Evolved (ATE). The page should also show what it gives over a row of ATE Advanced Planters, in the owner's words: "Easier automation and handling of outputs, power, and easier viewing of what planter has what seeds, soil, and upgrades."
14	
15	## Goals
16	
17	1. **Summary.** The CurseForge and Modrinth summary line is exactly: `Build Agritech: Evolved planters into one multiblock with shared power, fertilizer and outputs`. It is 94 characters, and both sites allow 256 (owner, 2026-11-03).
18	2. **Logo.** The logo is mockup C from the brainstorm: a small isometric multiblock drawn from the mod's own block textures, on a transparent background. A Planter Core sits in the middle, with Planter Power, Planter Fertilizer and Planter Export Blocks behind it and Planter Blocks in front. The mockup is `.superpowers/brainstorm/364-1793491880/content/logo-c.png`, and the script that drew it is copied next to it as `logos.py`. It has to read at CurseForge's 256x256 icon size on both a dark and a light background.
19	3. **Project page.** One markdown text is used for both CurseForge and Modrinth. Top to bottom:
20	   1. a banner image at the top, where Oritech shows its build render;
21	   2. a one or two sentence pitch;
22	   3. a "Features" bullet list, like Oritech's "Features include";
23	   4. one section per feature, each with a heading, about two sentences, and an in-game screenshot.
24	
25	   The page uses real text only, never text drawn into images. There is no badge row, because both sites already show source, issue, wiki and license links. The sections are "Build it your way", "See every planter at once", "One connection runs it all", "AE2 and Applied Flux", and "Guide and Jade".
26	4. **README.md.** It is written for people browsing the source repo, opening issues, or reading the code. It has:
27	   - logo C, the summary, a short description and a few screenshots;
28	   - links to the guide, to issues, and to CONTRIBUTING.md and DEVELOPMENT.md;
29	   - the license and the ATE texture credit.
30	
31	   The player reference leaves the README: the block table, building rules, how a Planter Block grows, the cloche rule, recipes, AE2 and Applied Flux details, the Logistics Networks numbers, the server config table and the abbreviations table. Anything the guide in `wiki/` doesn't already cover is added to the guide first, so nothing is lost.
32	5. **CONTRIBUTING.md.** It follows the Contributing section of Oritech's README:
33	   - contributions are welcome;
34	   - for content or balance changes, ask first in an issue, because the owner has a specific vision for the mod;
35	   - one pull request per change;
36	   - search open and closed issues before opening a new one.
37	
38	   It says nothing about translations, since the mod is English only for now.
39	6. **GitHub templates in `.github/`**, modeled on Oritech's:
40	   - **Bug report form.** It asks for:
41	     - the issue and the expected result;
42	     - steps to reproduce;
43	     - the Minecraft, NeoForge, Modular Planters and ATE versions;
44	     - other relevant mods and their versions (AE2, Applied Flux, Jade, Productive Farming, Logistics Networks);
45	     - a log link (mclo.gs, gist or pastebin).
46	   - **Feature request form.**
47	   - **`config.yml`.** Blank issues are disabled. The only contact link is to the guide, because there is no Discord or GitHub Discussions.
48	   - **Pull request template.** It asks what changed and why, the related issue, and how the change was tested: GameTests (`./gradlew runGameTestServer`), plus in game and on a dedicated server when client code is involved.
49	7. **DEVELOPMENT.md.** It covers setting up the project locally:
50	   - JDK 25 and the Gradle wrapper;
51	   - `./gradlew build`, `runClient`, `runServer`, `runGameTestServer`, `runData` and `test`;
52	   - the `-PnoJade`, `-PnoAe2` and `-PnoAppliedFlux` switches;
53	   - where the generated resources (`src/generated/resources`, from `runData`) and the guide pages (`wiki/`, copied into the jar by `processResources`) live;
54	   - the optional mods on the dev runtime and the versions they are pinned to, including Powah (with Cloth Config and GuideME) for fast FE in dev runs and its `-PnoPowah` switch, committed in e586fdb;
55	   - the `-PstructureLabJar=<path>` switch, which loads a local Structure Lab jar for taking world screenshots. Structure Lab is the owner's local build and isn't published, so DEVELOPMENT.md says it is optional and only for screenshots.
56	
57	## Non-goals
58

1	# Modular Planters plan 5: justfile, formatting hooks, CI and releases
2	
3	Date: 2026-11-03. Status: approved by the owner on 2026-11-03. A builder check was run, and its one open question (IDE settings) was answered by the owner.
4	
5	Choices marked **(my call)** were made by Claude, the assistant writing this, and haven't been confirmed by the owner yet. Everything else was decided by the owner during the brainstorm on 2026-11-03.
6	
7	## Why
8	
9	Plan 4 got the mod ready for CurseForge and Modrinth. Releasing still means building by hand, uploading the jar to two sites, and copying notes around. Formatting is unchecked, and nothing runs the tests on a push or a pull request. The owner wants:
10	- releases that happen by pushing a version tag;
11	- formatting that is checked automatically on every commit;
12	- one `just` command for each common task.
13	
14	## Goals
15	
16	### 1. Releases start from a tag
17	
18	Pushing a tag such as `26.1.2-0.1.0` runs a release workflow. The tag is the Minecraft version, a hyphen, then the mod version, the pattern Logistics Networks uses (its tags are `26.1.2-1.13.0` and `1.21.1-1.17.2`). This leaves room for later releases for 26.3 or 1.21.1 from the same repo. Nothing is clicked in GitHub's web UI.
19	
20	**Release type.** A suffix on the tag sets the type on CurseForge and Modrinth:
21	- `26.1.2-0.1.0-alpha` is alpha;
22	- `26.1.2-0.1.0-beta` is beta;
23	- no suffix is a full release.
24	
25	**The release workflow, in order:**
26	1. **Check the version.** The tag must equal `<minecraft_version>-<mod_version>` from `gradle.properties`, where `mod_version` carries any `-alpha` or `-beta` suffix. If it doesn't, the workflow stops before building.
27	2. **Check the changelog.** `CHANGELOG.md` must have a section for this version, or the workflow stops before building.
28	3. **Build and test.** Build the jar, then run the unit tests (`./gradlew test`) and the GameTests (`./gradlew runGameTestServer`). If any fail, nothing is published.
29	4. **Publish.** Create the GitHub release with the jar attached, then upload the same jar to CurseForge and Modrinth. All three use the changelog section for this version as their notes. On CurseForge and Modrinth the file is set to:
30	   - game version 26.1.2 and loader NeoForge;
31	   - client and server;
32	   - Agritech: Evolved required, and AE2, Applied Flux, Jade, Oracle Index and Logistics Networks optional, on each site where the project exists. Logistics Networks is only on CurseForge.
33	5. **Tool.** Publishing uses Oritech's Gradle plugin, `me.modmuss50.mod-publish-plugin`. The same task can run locally as a dry run.
34	
35	**Jar name.** It becomes `modular_planters-<minecraft_version>-<mod_version>.jar`, for example `modular_planters-26.1.2-0.1.0.jar`. The version inside `neoforge.mods.toml` stays `mod_version`.
36	
37	**Tokens and project ids.**
38	- The CurseForge and Modrinth tokens are GitHub secrets.
39	- The two project ids go into `gradle.properties` once the owner creates the projects.
40	- While an id is empty, the workflow skips that site and still makes the GitHub release.
41	
42	### 2. A running changelog
43	
44	`CHANGELOG.md` has one section per version, headed `## 26.1.2-0.1.0`, newest first. The release takes only the section matching the tag. The owner chose this over Oritech's "next release only" file, knowing the file grows by a few lines per release and old sections can be trimmed.
45	
46	### 3. Formatting with prek
47	
48	`prek.toml` configures [prek](https://prek.j178.dev). The owner installs it once as a git pre-commit hook (`prek install`), and the build workflow runs it on every push and pull request.
49	
50	**Java.**
51	- `google-java-format` applies the Google Java Style Guide: 2-space indents and 100-character lines.
52	- The first run reformats every Java file in a commit of its own. The current code uses 4-space indents across 111 files and about 10,000 lines, with 245 lines over 120 characters.
53	- That commit's hash goes into `.git-blame-ignore-revs`, so `git blame` and GitHub's blame view skip it.
54	
55	**IDE settings.** A tracked `.editorconfig` (owner, 2026-11-03) sets Java to 2-space indents and a 100-column limit, so IntelliJ's own formatting matches google-java-format. `.idea/` stays gitignored. *(my call)* It also sets UTF-8, LF line endings and a final newline for every file except JSON, matching the hooks.
56	
57	**Markdown, YAML and JSON.** Prettier formats them.
58	
59	**Builtin hooks:**
60	- check-added-large-files;
61	- check-case-conflict;
62	- check-merge-conflict;
63	- detect-private-key;
64	- trailing-whitespace;
65	- end-of-file-fixer, skipping JSON (owner: "JSON can skip the 'file ends with newline' rule");
66	- check-toml and check-yaml.
67	
68	**Left alone by the formatters:**
69	- `src/generated/resources`, because `runData` writes it and the build workflow compares it with a fresh `runData` run;
70	- the guide's `.mdx` pages, because Prettier would turn the single quotes in `<CraftingRecipe slots={[...]}>` into double quotes, which `WikiStructureTest` reads, and Oracle Index uses its own MDX dialect;
71	- `graphify-out/`, because it is regenerated whole.
72	
73	The file opens with `minimum_prek_version` and the schemastore `#:schema` line.
74	
75	### 4. The build workflow
76	
77	It runs on every branch push and every pull request. *(my call)* Newer runs on the same branch cancel older ones. It does these steps:
78	1. Run prek on all files, so formatting problems fail CI even from contributors who never installed prek.
79	2. Run `./gradlew runData`, and fail if it leaves any change. This works the way AE2's build does.
80	3. Build, run the unit tests, and run the GameTests.
81	4. Upload the jar as a workflow artifact.
82	
83	### 5. A justfile
84	
85	The recipes are listed below. In the file, the default recipe lists them all, and each recipe has a `[doc]` line and a `[group]`. The file sets `set shell := ["bash", "-euo", "pipefail", "-c"]` and opens with a header comment.
86	- **gradle:**
87	  - `build`, `test`, `gametest`, and `check`, which runs both kinds of tests;
88	  - `client` and `server`, which pass extra flags through (`just client -PnoAe2`);
89	  - `data`, which runs `runData`.
90	- **lint:**
91	  - `lint` runs `prek run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure`;
92	  - `fmt` runs `google-java-format` and Prettier so they fix files in place.
93	- **media:**
94	  - `logo` runs `uv run tools/render_logo.py`;
95	  - `compress *files` runs `pngquant --quality=80-95 --speed 1 --strip --force --ext .png` and then `oxipng -o 4 --strip safe` on the named PNGs.
96	- **release:**
97	  - `changelog <version>` prints that version's section of `CHANGELOG.md`;
98	  - `release-check` runs the release workflow's checks for the version in `gradle.properties` (tag format, versions, changelog section), plus a publish dry run.
99	
100	The workflows don't call `just`. They run the same Gradle tasks and the same bash scripts under `tools/` directly. The changelog extraction and the version checks live in those scripts, so `just` and CI can't drift apart.
101	
102	### 6. Docs
103	
104	DEVELOPMENT.md and CONTRIBUTING.md switch to the `just` commands and say to run `prek install` once. DEVELOPMENT.md documents the release steps:
105	1. Bump `mod_version`.
106	2. Add the changelog section.
107	3. Run `just release-check`.
108	4. Push the tag.
109	
110	It also lists the secrets and project ids the workflow needs.
111	
112	## Non-goals
113	
114	- Publishing to a maven repository, Crowdin, Discord announcements, or signing.
115	- Branches or builds for 26.3 or 1.21.1. The tag pattern only leaves room for them.
116	- Branch protection rules and GitHub repository settings.
117	- Creating the CurseForge and Modrinth projects. The owner does that, then fills in the ids and secrets.
118	
119	## Anti-goals
120	
121	- **Publishing a jar whose tests failed,** or whose version doesn't match its tag.
122	- **A half-done release nobody notices.** If one upload fails after another succeeded, the run fails visibly. Re-running it must not upload duplicates to the sites that already succeeded.
123	- **Any mention of ARC,** the folder of the owner's older repositories that the justfile and `prek.toml` style was taken from, in any committed file, comment or commit message (owner, 2026-11-03).
124	- **Formatters rewriting generated files or the guide's `.mdx` pages.**
125	
126	## Constraints
127	
128	- No unicode em or en dashes in any new text.
129	- Comments follow the owner's rules: necessary, full plain sentences, complete.
130	- Scripts in the repo are bash, falling back to POSIX sh.
131	- The release workflow and `just release-check` must read the versions from `gradle.properties` the same way.
132	- The existing tests stay green. That includes `ProjectDocsTest`, which needs a git clone and skips its link check without one.
133	
134	## Calls left to the builder, already made
135	
136	- **(my call)** **Secret names:** `CURSEFORGE_API_KEY` and `MODRINTH_API_KEY`, as Oritech names them.
137	- **(my call)** **Project id properties:** `curseforge_project_id` and `modrinth_project_id` in `gradle.properties`, empty for now.
138	- **(my call)** **Action pinning:** third-party GitHub actions are pinned to full commit SHAs with the version in a comment. The `actions/*` ones use major version tags.
139	- **(my call)** **Running prek in CI:** CI runs prek with its official action, `j178/prek-action`.
140	- **(my call)** **Tool choice:** the builder picks which prek hook repos provide `google-java-format` and Prettier. They must work on the owner's Mac (Homebrew, a JDK on the PATH) and in CI without manual installs beyond what the workflow sets up.
141	- **(my call)** **Recovering from a failed release.** Each destination (GitHub release, CurseForge, Modrinth) is its own job, after one shared build-and-test job. A failed upload is retried with GitHub's "Re-run failed jobs", which reruns only the failed destination, so nothing is uploaded twice. If the fix needs a code change, the owner releases a new version. A pushed tag is never moved. DEVELOPMENT.md says this.
142	- **(my call)** **Which mods load during the GameTests.** Both workflows run the GameTests three ways: with every dev mod, with `-PnoAe2`, and with `-PnoAppliedFlux`. This follows the project's recorded testing rule for AE2 and Applied Flux code. Without it, a crash for players without AE2 would never fail a test. It costs extra minutes per run.
143	- **(my call)** **The release repeats the build checks.** The release workflow also runs prek and the `runData` check, through the same reusable workflow the build workflow calls. That way a tag pushed together with its commit can't publish stale generated data before the build workflow has finished.
144	- **(my call)** **The mods.toml template.** `check-toml` skips `src/main/templates/META-INF/neoforge.mods.toml`, which isn't valid TOML until Gradle fills in its `${...}` placeholders.
145	- **(my call)** **The first changelog section:** `CHANGELOG.md` starts with a `0.1.0` section summarizing the features from the project page. The owner reviews it before the first tag.

380	# Modular Planters Plan 5: Justfile, Formatting Hooks, CI and Releases Implementation Plan
381	> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.
382	**Goal:** Releases happen by pushing a `26.1.2-<mod version>` tag. prek and CI check formatting and tests on every push and pull request. A justfile wraps the common commands.
383	**Architecture:**
384	- **Release scripts.** Two bash scripts in `tools/` hold the release rules, and the justfile, the workflows and Gradle all call them: `changelog-section.sh` prints one version's notes, and `check-release.sh` checks a tag against `gradle.properties` and `CHANGELOG.md`.
385	- **Publishing.** `me.modmuss50.mod-publish-plugin` does the uploads, with one task per site. Each site gets its own workflow job, so "Re-run failed jobs" retries only the failed one.
386	- **Shared checks.** A reusable workflow (`checks.yml`) holds prek, the `runData` check, the build and the GameTest matrix. Both the build workflow and the release workflow call it.
387	**Tech Stack:** Gradle 9.2.1, ModDevGradle, `me.modmuss50.mod-publish-plugin` 2.2.1, GitHub Actions, prek 0.5.x, google-java-format (through `macisamuele/language-formatters-pre-commit-hooks` `pretty-format-java`), Prettier (`rbubley/mirrors-prettier`), actionlint, shellcheck, just, JUnit 5.
388	**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-03-modular-planters-plan-5-ci-release-design.md` (approved 2026-11-03).
389	## Global Constraints
390	- **Tag and version format:**
391	  - The tag is `<minecraft_version>-<mod_version>`, for example `26.1.2-0.1.0`.
392	  - A `-alpha` or `-beta` suffix on `mod_version` makes the release alpha or beta. No suffix makes it a full release.
393	  - The jar is `modular_planters-<minecraft_version>-<mod_version>.jar`.
394	  - The `version` inside `neoforge.mods.toml` stays `mod_version`.
395	- **`CHANGELOG.md`:** one `## <tag>` section per version, newest first. The release notes are that section's body.
396	- **No mention of ARC** in any committed file, comment or commit message. `git grep -nw ARC` must print nothing.
397	- **Comments:** no unicode em or en dashes. Comments are necessary, full plain sentences, and complete.
398	- **Shell:** scripts are bash, falling back to POSIX sh.
399	- **Secrets and ids:**
400	  - The secrets are `CURSEFORGE_API_KEY` and `MODRINTH_API_KEY`.

# Modular Planters Plan 3: Jade and the Guide Implementation Plan
> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.
**Goal:** Add the optional Jade tooltips for the core and the planter block, and the Oracle Index guide book with every page the spec lists.
**Architecture:** The Jade data and lines are built by a Jade-free class (`jade/JadeInfo`) that GameTests can call; thin Jade providers wrap it and are only loaded by Jade. The guide is resources only: MDX pages in a top-level `wiki/` folder in the moddedmc.wiki layout, copied into `assets/oracle_index/books/modular_planters` by `processResources`, and checked by JUnit tests that read the folder and the generated recipe JSON.
**Tech Stack:** NeoForge 26.1.2 (ModDevGradle 2.0.141), Java 25, Jade 26.1 API (`snownee.jade.api`), Oracle Index 2.0.0 book format, JUnit 5 with Gson, NeoForge GameTests.
**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-28-modular-planters-design.md` (sections "Jade" and "Guide"). Plans 1 and 2 are in the same folder. Decisions made without the owner are listed in `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-31-modular-planters-plan-3-todos.md`; the owner confirms them later, and a changed answer becomes a follow-up task.
## Global Constraints
- Platform: NeoForge 26.1.2, Java 25. Mod id `modular_planters`, package `io.github.julianperge.modular_planters`.
- Jade and Oracle Index are optional. The mod has to load and work with either missing. Every GameTest passes with `-PnoJade`.
- Oracle Index needs no code: the guide is resources only, so the build gets no Oracle Index dependency.
- No unicode characters such as em dashes anywhere: code, comments, lang, pages.
- A comment must be necessary (why, cross-file links, intentional absences), a full plain sentence, and complete. Few comments.
- MIT. No code copied from ModularBees. Oritech (`~/DEV/git_repos/minecraft-mods/Oritech`) is the working example for the guide setup and the Jade plugin shape.
- ATE's numbers are never hard-coded in code. Pages may quote ATE's defaults as examples, labeled as defaults, the way the README does.
- `README.md` is the source of truth for player-facing rules; guide pages adapt its sections and must not contradict it.
- Never push. Commit only with the owner's approval for plan 3.
- Subagent prompts that explore code include the project rule: run `graphify query "<question>"` before grep or file reads, and run `graphify update .` after code changes.
- Full verification: `./gradlew test`, `./gradlew runGameTestServer`, and the same GameTests with `-PnoAe2`, `-PnoAppliedFlux` and `-PnoJade`.

1. A server without Jade and a client with it: the client gets empty server data and must show no lines instead of throwing. Pinned in Task 1 (`emptyServerDataShowsNoLines`).

Before its first scan a core shows "Waiting for chunks to load" because `lastScan` starts as WAITING_FOR_CHUNKS; no test pins that case.
4. A recipe changed in datagen without the guide page: the page would teach the wrong recipe. Pinned in Task 4 (`blockPagesMatchTheirRecipes`).
5. A `_meta.json` entry or `ModAsset` pointing at a missing file: Oracle Index shows a broken page. Pinned in Task 3 (`metaFilesListEveryPageAndNothingElse`, `everyModAssetExists`).

# Modular Planters Plan 4: Project Pages, Logo and Contributor Docs Implementation Plan
> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.
**Goal:** Ship the CurseForge/Modrinth page text and images, the logo, a README for repo visitors, CONTRIBUTING.md, DEVELOPMENT.md and GitHub templates, and move the README's player reference into the guide.
**Architecture:** Everything is files in the repo. Page images live in `docs/media/`. The page text is `docs/description.md`, and it links its images by raw GitHub URLs on `main`. Two JUnit tests guard the docs: `ProjectDocsTest` checks every new doc for unicode dashes, short block names and broken links, and `LogoTest` checks the logo files and mod metadata. `WikiStructureTest` gains a check that the guide names every server config option.
**Tech Stack:** Markdown, GitHub issue forms (YAML), JUnit 5 (`./gradlew test`), Pillow through a PEP 723 script (`uv run`), Gradle `localRuntime` dev mods.
**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-31-modular-planters-plan-4-pages-design.md` (approved 2026-11-03). Its "Pictures chosen by the owner" table fixes every image.
## Global Constraints
- No unicode em or en dashes in any new or changed text.
- Player-facing text names blocks by their in-game names: Modular Planter Core, Modular Planter Block, Modular Planter Power Block, Modular Planter Fertilizer Block, Modular Planter Export Block, Modular Planter ME Block, Modular Planter Frame. Never the short "Planter Core" or "Planter Block" forms. Lowercase generic words ("power blocks") are fine.
- ATE's names: "Advanced Planter", "upgrades", "Speed Upgrade MK3".
- Summary line, exact: `Build Agritech: Evolved planters into one multiblock with shared power, fertilizer and outputs`
- Every mechanics statement must match the current code and guide. The Modular Planter Core screen shows each Modular Planter Block's seed, growing count, upgrade coverage, status and position. It does not show soil.
- No text drawn into images. No badge row on the page.
- Raw image URL prefix: `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/julian-perge/ModularPlanters/main/`
- Commit subjects use the repo's `type: lowercase subject` form, with no AI attribution trailers.
- Work on branch `plan-4-pages`, cut from `main`.
## Review Focus
1. A page image URL that 404s once pasted into CurseForge or Modrinth, because the raw URL's path doesn't match a committed file. `ProjectDocsTest.linksResolve` maps raw and blob URLs back to repo paths (Task 4).
2. A short block name ("Planter Core") or an em dash slipping into new text. `ProjectDocsTest.noUnicodeDashes` and `ProjectDocsTest.blockNamesAreInGame` (Task 4; Tasks 5 to 7 add their files to its list).
3. A README fact lost when the player reference moves out. `WikiStructureTest.guideCoversEveryServerConfigOption` (Task 2) plus the move checklist in Task 5.
4. A new dev mod (Oracle Index, Architectury, Logistics Networks) breaking GameTests or client start. Task 1 runs GameTests with and without each switch.
5. A placeholder left in the page after the owner's shots arrive. `ProjectDocsTest.noShotPlaceholdersLeft` (Task 8).
---
### Task 1: Oracle Index and Logistics Networks on the dev runtime
**Files:**
- Modify: `build.gradle` (dependencies block, next to the Powah block)
**Interfaces:**
- Produces: `-PnoOracleIndex` and `-PnoLogisticsNetworks` switches. Task 7 documents them.
- [ ] **Step 1: Cut the branch:** `git switch -c plan-4-pages main`
- [ ] **Step 2: Add the dependencies**, each in its own guarded block with a one-line comment saying why it is there (screenshots and checks in dev, no code uses it):
  - `noOracleIndex`: `localRuntime "maven.modrinth:oracle-index:2.0.0"` and `localRuntime "maven.modrinth:architectury-api:20.1.17+neoforge"`. Oracle Index requires Architectury.
  - `noLogisticsNetworks`: `localRuntime "curse.maven:logistics-networks-1448257:9115811"`. This is CurseForge project 1448257, file 9115811, `logisticsnetworks-26.1.2-1.13.0.jar`, the ATM11 version.
- [ ] **Step 3: Check they resolve:** `./gradlew dependencies --configuration runtimeClasspath --console=plain -q | rg 'oracle-index|architectury|logistics-networks'`. Expected: three lines, none marked `FAILED`.
- [ ] **Step 4: Run GameTests:** `./gradlew runGameTestServer --console=plain | rg 'required tests passed|failed'`. Expected: `All 126 required tests passed`. Repeat with `-PnoOracleIndex -PnoLogisticsNetworks`. Expected: the same.
- [ ] **Step 5: Check the client loads them:** run `./gradlew runClient --console=plain` in the background. Wait until `run/logs/latest.log` has `Reloading ResourceManager`. That line must list `mod/oracle_index`, `mod/architectury` and `mod/logisticsnetworks`. Then stop the client.
- [ ] **Step 6: Commit:** `chore: add oracle index and logistics networks to dev runs`
### Task 2: Move the README's missing player facts into the guide
**Files:**
- Create: `wiki/docs/config.mdx`, `wiki/docs/jade.mdx`
- Modify: `wiki/docs/overview.mdx`, `wiki/docs/_meta.json`
- Test: `src/test/java/io/github/julianperge/modular_planters/wiki/WikiStructureTest.java`
The guide already covers the blocks, building rules, growing, the cloche, recipes, AE2 and Applied Flux, and Logistics Networks. Four README facts are missing:
- the server config table;
- the Jade section;
- the requirements (Minecraft 26.1.2, NeoForge 26.1.2.116 or newer);
- "recipes are datapack JSON, so a pack can replace them".
- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test** `guideCoversEveryServerConfigOption` in `WikiStructureTest`:
  - Read `src/main/java/io/github/julianperge/modular_planters/MPConfig.java` and match every `defineInRange\("(\w+)", ([\d_]+), (\d+), ([\w.]+)\)`.
  - Assert there are 3 matches.
  - For each match, assert `wiki/docs/config.mdx` contains the option name in backticks, and its default with underscores removed and US thousands separators (`24`, `4,000,000`, `20`).

# Modular Planters Plan 5: Justfile, Formatting Hooks, CI and Releases Implementation Plan
> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.
**Goal:** Releases happen by pushing a `26.1.2-<mod version>` tag. prek and CI check formatting and tests on every push and pull request. A justfile wraps the common commands.
**Architecture:**
- **Release scripts.** Two bash scripts in `tools/` hold the release rules, and the justfile, the workflows and Gradle all call them: `changelog-section.sh` prints one version's notes, and `check-release.sh` checks a tag against `gradle.properties` and `CHANGELOG.md`.
- **Publishing.** `me.modmuss50.mod-publish-plugin` does the uploads, with one task per site. Each site gets its own workflow job, so "Re-run failed jobs" retries only the failed one.
- **Shared checks.** A reusable workflow (`checks.yml`) holds prek, the `runData` check, the build and the GameTest matrix. Both the build workflow and the release workflow call it.
**Tech Stack:** Gradle 9.2.1, ModDevGradle, `me.modmuss50.mod-publish-plugin` 2.2.1, GitHub Actions, prek 0.5.x, google-java-format (through `macisamuele/language-formatters-pre-commit-hooks` `pretty-format-java`), Prettier (`rbubley/mirrors-prettier`), actionlint, shellcheck, just, JUnit 5.
**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-03-modular-planters-plan-5-ci-release-design.md` (approved 2026-11-03).
## Global Constraints
- **Tag and version format:**
  - The tag is `<minecraft_version>-<mod_version>`, for example `26.1.2-0.1.0`.
  - A `-alpha` or `-beta` suffix on `mod_version` makes the release alpha or beta. No suffix makes it a full release.
  - The jar is `modular_planters-<minecraft_version>-<mod_version>.jar`.
  - The `version` inside `neoforge.mods.toml` stays `mod_version`.
- **`CHANGELOG.md`:** one `## <tag>` section per version, newest first. The release notes are that section's body.
- **No mention of ARC** in any committed file, comment or commit message. `git grep -nw ARC` must print nothing.
- **Comments:** no unicode em or en dashes. Comments are necessary, full plain sentences, and complete.
- **Shell:** scripts are bash, falling back to POSIX sh.
- **Secrets and ids:**
  - The secrets are `CURSEFORGE_API_KEY` and `MODRINTH_API_KEY`.
