=========== 2026-10-28-modular-planters-plan-1-working-multiblock.md
# Modular Planters, plan 1 of 3: the working multiblock
> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.
**Goal:** Build the Modular Planters mod up to a multiblock the owner can run in FTB Evolution 2 from one Logistics Networks node on the core: every block except the ME block, the planter growth that matches Powered Planters seed for seed, the planter and core screens, recipes and textures.
**Architecture:** All growth, coverage, cloche and structure math lives in `logic/`, a package with no Minecraft or NeoForge imports, tested with plain JUnit. The block entities only move items and energy, fire ATE's events and call into `logic/`. The core drives the whole multiblock from its own server tick: it scans the structure, builds the power, fertilizer and output pools, and ticks the planter blocks in block-position order. NeoForge GameTests cover everything that needs a world.
**Tech Stack:** Java 25, NeoForge 26.1.2.121, ModDevGradle 2.0.141, Gradle 9.2.1, Agritech: Evolved 2.2.0.6 (from CurseForge Maven), JUnit 5.13.4, NeoForge GameTests.
**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-28-modular-planters-design.md` (approved 2026-10-28). Background research is in `NOTES.md`.
**The three plans:**
1. This plan: the working multiblock.
2. The ME block, with AE2 and Applied Flux. It also adds the ME interval to the server config, the ME recipe, ME status on the core screen, and the ME path in `OutputSink` and `FertilizerPool`.
3. The Jade plugin and the Oracle Index guide.
Plans 2 and 3 get written after this one lands, against the real code.
## Global Constraints
- **Paths:** the repository root is `~/DEV/git_repos/minecraft-mods/ate-planter-multiblock` while this plan runs. It gets renamed to `ModularPlanters` after the plan is done. In this plan, `J/` means `src/main/java/io/github/julianperge/modular_planters/`, `T/` means `src/test/java/io/github/julianperge/modular_planters/`, and `R/` means `src/main/resources/`.
- **Identity:** mod id `modular_planters`, name `Modular Planters`, package `io.github.julianperge.modular_planters`, license MIT, version `0.1.0`.
- **Versions:** Minecraft `26.1.2`, NeoForge `26.1.2.121`, Java 25, ModDevGradle `2.0.141`, Gradle wrapper `9.2.1`. Copy `build.gradle`'s shape from `~/DEV/git_repos/minecraft-mods/AgritechEvolved/build.gradle`.
- **ATE dependency:** `implementation "curse.maven:agritech-evolved-1287394:9155589"` (2.2.0.6) from `https://www.cursemaven.com`. In `neoforge.mods.toml` it's `type="required"`, `versionRange="[2.2.0,)"`, `ordering="AFTER"`.
- **ATE numbers:** production code reads every ATE number through `com.misterd.agritechevolved.Config` getters, each tick, via `AteBridge.numbers()`. ATE's default numbers appear only in test code (`T/logic/AteDefaults.java`), never in `src/main`.
- **No copied code:**
  - ModularBees (LGPL-3.0), Logistics Networks (All Rights Reserved) and NeoForge's testframework (LGPL-2.1) may be read for ideas only.
  - ATE's textures (MIT) are adapted, and `../../../LICENSE-ATE.md` ships in the jar.
- **The `logic` package** imports nothing from `net.minecraft`, `net.neoforged`, `com.mojang` or `com.misterd`. Its tests are plain JUnit, run by `./gradlew test`.
- **Never lose or duplicate items.** When there's nowhere to put outputs, planter blocks wait. Breaking a block drops everything it holds, except the power block, which keeps its energy in the dropped item.
- **Logistics Networks:** no block in this mod goes in any `logisticsnetwork:blacklist/*` tag.
- **Comments** follow the owner's rule. Write one only when the code can't say it (a reason, a link to another file, an intentional absence), as a full plain sentence that says what actually happens. Otherwise leave it out.
- **Commits:** the owner approved committing for this plan on 2026-10-28. Each task ends with a commit on the branch `plan-1-working-multiblock`. Never push. Commit subjects are lowercase `type: subject` with no period.
- **Text in game** (lang strings, tooltips) uses no em dashes or semicolons.
## Review Focus
These are the five inputs the spec implies but doesn't spell out, most likely to bite first. Each one has a test in the task that owns the code.
1. **Server restart mid-growth.** Per-seed progress, ready flags, seed data, cloche remainders and held outputs all survive a save and load exactly. Test: `planter_state_survives_save_and_load` (Task 12).
2. **A part's chunk unloads while the multiblock is formed**, for example a build across a chunk border when the player walks away. The multiblock pauses without unforming, and nothing is lost. Test: `unloadedPartMakesTheScanWait` (Task 5), plus a manual check in Task 16.

questions.question: Architecture ADRs. Which should I write? All four are confirmed against the current code.

options.label: AE2 stays behind MeLink (Recommended)
options.description: The multiblock talks to ME only through an AE2-free interface, and all AE2 and Applied Flux classes sit in the ae2 package behind isLoaded, so the mod loads without them. This is the seam codebase-design will look at.

options.label: Pure logic package (Recommended)
options.description: All growth, coverage, cloche and structure math is in logic/ with no Minecraft, NeoForge or ATE imports, so plain JUnit covers it and block entities only move items and energy. Confirmed: no such imports exist.

options.label: The core drives every tick
options.description: The Core scans, builds the pools and ticks every Modular Planter Block in position order from its own server tick, instead of each block ticking itself.

options.label: ATE numbers are read live
options.description: Every ATE number is read each tick through ATE's Config getters via AteBridge and never copied, so the mod follows each pack's ATE config. ATE defaults appear only in tests.

questions.question: Behavior and scope ADRs. Which should I write?

options.label: ME refills power every tick
options.description: With Applied Flux the ME block fills the power blocks' free room each tick (up to 4,000,000 RF each once). The earlier rule refilled only last tick's demand and left the bars showing 0; changed after in-game testing 2026-10-30.

options.label: Free-form shape, 24-part cap
options.description: Any face-connected shape forms a multiblock, with a configurable cap of 24 parts, instead of a fixed blueprint. The cap and the two-core and second-ME rules replace shape checking.

options.label: No Logistics Networks block
options.description: One ordinary LN node on the Core runs the whole multiblock through the Doorway, so the mod has no LN code and no block of its own for it.

options.label: Pause, don't unform, on unloaded chunks
options.description: While any part's chunk is unloaded the multiblock waits without unforming, so contents and progress are never lost or duplicated.

questions.question: Process and compatibility ADRs. Which should I write?

options.label: Save keys and ids never renamed
options.description: Save keys and registry ids keep their old names even when player-facing terms change, so the key `soil_and_modules` outlived the rename to upgrades.

options.label: Release tags are <mc>-<mod>
options.description: Tags like 26.1.2-0.1.0 (the Logistics Networks pattern) leave room for 26.3 or 1.21.1 releases from one repo. A pushed tag is never moved, and each site is its own job so a failed upload re-runs alone.

options.label: One reformat commit, history never rewritten
options.description: Java was reformatted to google-java-format in a single commit that .git-blame-ignore-revs hides, so merged history must never be squashed or rebased.

options.label: GameTests run three ways in CI
options.description: CI runs them with all mods, with -PnoAe2 and with -PnoAppliedFlux, costing extra minutes, so a crash for players without AE2 fails a test. Note: CI does not run -PnoJade, though plan 3 required it.

input.content:
# AE2 and Applied Flux stay behind MeLink

The mod must load and work with AE2, Applied Flux or both missing, and both are compile-time only dependencies. The multiblock code talks to ME only through `MeLink`, an interface with no AE2 types, and every class that touches AE2 sits in the `ae2` package, reached only behind a `ModList` loaded check. `FluxBridge` is the one class that touches Applied Flux.

The ME block's registration, item, recipe and loot table exist only when AE2 is installed, and generated data that references AE2 carries a `mod_loaded` condition. The pools and the Core can be tested with a fake `MeLink` and no AE2 on the classpath.

The ME block's registration, item, recipe and loot table exist only when AE2 is installed, and generated data that references AE2 carries a `mod_loaded` condition. The pools and the Core can be tested with a fake `MeLink` and no AE2 on the classpath.

input.content:
# Growth and structure math lives in a package with no Minecraft imports

All growth, coverage, cloche and structure math is in `logic/`, which imports nothing from `net.minecraft`, `net.neoforged`, `com.mojang` or ATE. Plain JUnit tests cover it and run with `./gradlew test`, while block entities only move items and energy, fire ATE's events and call into `logic/`. Anything that needs a world is covered by GameTests instead.

ATE's numbers reach `logic/` as a plain value object that tests can fill with ATE's defaults.

input.content:
# The ME block refills power blocks every tick

With Applied Flux, the ME block fills the Power Blocks' free room from the network's FE each tick, before the Modular Planter Blocks run. Filling empty Power Blocks takes up to their capacity, 4,000,000 RF each, out of the network once. The first rule refilled only what the Modular Planter Blocks asked for the tick before, and in-game testing on 2026-10-30 showed the Power Blocks then always read 0 and looked broken, so the owner changed it.

input.content:
# Any face-connected shape forms a multiblock

The multiblock is the Core plus every part connected to it face to face, directly or through other parts, with no fixed blueprint. Instead of checking a shape, the Core enforces a part cap (24 by default, in the server config, Frames included), the required parts (a Power, an Export and a Planter Block), and at most one second Core or ME block. The guide's example builds are only examples.

The cost is that the Core has to explain why it did not form, which is why a Problem names the cause and the block's position.

input.content:
# The multiblock pauses, instead of unforming, when a part's chunk is unloaded

A build can cross a chunk border, and the player can walk away from half of it. While any part's chunk is unloaded the Core waits without unforming, every block keeps its contents and every seed keeps its progress, and nothing is lost or duplicated. Treating the missing part as a broken shape would stop the Modular Planter Blocks and could change what they hold.

input.content:
# Save keys and registry ids are never renamed

Renaming a save key or registry id breaks existing worlds, so player-facing words can change while stored names stay. Modules became upgrades in the code, docs and screens on 2026-10-31, but the save key `soil_and_modules` kept its old name. ATE's own names, such as its module tags and config getters, stay as ATE has them.

input.content:
# Release tags are the Minecraft version, then the mod version

A tag such as `26.1.2-0.1.0` is `<minecraft_version>-<mod_version>`, the pattern Logistics Networks uses, which leaves room for 26.3 or 1.21.1 releases from the same repo. The release workflow rejects a tag that does not match `gradle.properties`, and a `-alpha` or `-beta` suffix on `mod_version` sets the release type.

A pushed tag is never moved. The GitHub release, CurseForge and Modrinth are separate jobs, so "Re-run failed jobs" repeats only the one that failed and nothing is uploaded twice, and a fix that needs code is released as a new version.

input.content:
# GameTests run three ways in CI

Both the Build and Release workflows run the GameTests with every dev mod, with `-PnoAe2`, and with `-PnoAppliedFlux`. Without the variants, a crash for players who lack AE2 or Applied Flux would never fail a test, because the dev runtime includes both. It costs extra minutes per run, and `just check` runs the same three.

CI does not run `-PnoJade`, so after changing the Jade integration run `just gametest -PnoJade` locally.

I wrote eight more ADRs, 0005 to 0012, so `docs/adr/` now has twelve. They're uncommitted, and `prek` passed with no unicode dashes.

I read the three design specs and todo lists in full. I read plans 3 to 5 as prose with the code blocks stripped. For plans 1 and 2 I read only the preamble and constraint sections, plus the lines that give a reason or ruling. The step-by-step task code in plans 1 and 2 was not read.

I found twelve candidates and you picked eight. The new ADRs cover:
- AE2 and Applied Flux stay behind `MeLink`.
- The growth and structure math sits in a package with no Minecraft imports. I confirmed no such imports exist.
- The ME block refills the Power Blocks every tick.
- Any face-connected shape forms a multiblock, with a 24-part cap.
- The multiblock pauses, rather than unforming, when a part's chunk is unloaded.
- Save keys and ids are never renamed.
- Release tags are the Minecraft version then the mod version.
- GameTests run three ways in CI.

I did not write ADRs for the four you skipped: the Core driving every tick, ATE numbers read live, no Logistics Networks block, and the reformat commit with no history rewriting. The handoff lists them.

**New finding:** CI does not run `-PnoJade`, although plan 3 required every GameTest to pass with it. ADR 0012 says to run `just gametest -PnoJade` locally after Jade changes. Do you want a fourth CI variant added instead? That would be a workflow change, so I haven't made it.

**Next:** does the glossary and the twelve-ADR set look right? Then I can start `codebase-design`, which proposes deepening opportunities and doesn't edit code.

name: Checks

on:
  workflow_call:

permissions:
  contents: read

defaults:
  run:
    shell: bash

jobs:
  prek:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      # google-java-format uses the javac parser of the JDK it runs on, so it needs JDK 25 to read this code.
      - uses: actions/setup-java@v6
        with:
          distribution: microsoft
          java-version: "25"
      - uses: j178/prek-action@44924fe9ef4a6f88253c4b6b1bf11c689d3ce53d # v3.1.0

  generated-data:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-java@v6
        with:
          distribution: microsoft
          java-version: "25"
      - uses: gradle/actions/setup-gradle@8da46b539cd8fe6ab27ca75128919a18d757604c # v6.4.1
        with:
          cache-provider: basic
      - run: ./gradlew runData
      - name: Check that the generated data is committed
        run: |
          if [ -n "$(git status --porcelain src/generated)" ]; then
            git status --short src/generated
            echo "::error::runData changed src/generated. Run ./gradlew runData and commit the result."
            exit 1
          fi

  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-java@v6
        with:
          distribution: microsoft
          java-version: "25"
      - uses: gradle/actions/setup-gradle@8da46b539cd8fe6ab27ca75128919a18d757604c # v6.4.1
        with:
          cache-provider: basic
      - run: ./gradlew build
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: jar
          path: build/libs/*.jar
          if-no-files-found: error

  gametest:
    name: gametest ${{ matrix.flags }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        flags: ["", "-PnoAe2", "-PnoAppliedFlux"]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-java@v6
        with:
          distribution: microsoft
          java-version: "25"
      - uses: gradle/actions/setup-gradle@8da46b539cd8fe6ab27ca75128919a18d757604c # v6.4.1
        with:
          cache-provider: basic
      - run: ./gradlew runGameTestServer ${{ matrix.flags }} | tee gametest.log
      # Each flag leaves some GameTests out, and new GameTests change the count, so the check matches any count.
      - name: Check that every required GameTest passed
        run: grep -E 'All [0-9]+ required tests passed' gametest.log

# Local shortcuts for building, testing, formatting and releasing Modular Planters. `just` lists them, and `just <recipe>` runs one.
#
# CI does not call just. The workflows in .github/workflows run the same Gradle tasks and tools/ scripts directly.

set shell := ["bash", "-euo", "pipefail", "-c"]

# Recipe arguments arrive as $1, $2 and so on, so variadic recipes forward them with "$@" and keep each argument intact.
set positional-arguments

[private]
default:
    @just --list --unsorted

# Recipes that call tools outside the JDK depend on this, so a missing tool stops the recipe before it starts. DEVELOPMENT.md says how to install each one.
[private]
require +tools:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    missing=()
    for tool in "$@"; do
        command -v "$tool" >/dev/null || missing+=("$tool")
    done
    if [ ${#missing[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
        echo "error: missing ${missing[*]}. See the Setup section of DEVELOPMENT.md." >&2
        exit 1
    fi

[doc('Compile, run the unit tests and build the jar into build/libs/')]
[group('gradle')]
build:
    ./gradlew build

[doc('Run the unit tests in src/test')]
[group('gradle')]
test:
    ./gradlew test

[doc('Run the in-game tests on a headless server, for example: just gametest -PnoAe2')]
[group('gradle')]
gametest *flags:
    ./gradlew runGameTestServer "$@"

[doc('Run the unit tests, then the in-game tests with all dev mods, without AE2 and without Applied Flux, the three ways CI runs them')]
[group('gradle')]
check:
    ./gradlew test
    ./gradlew runGameTestServer
    ./gradlew runGameTestServer -PnoAe2
    ./gradlew runGameTestServer -PnoAppliedFlux

[doc('Start a dev client, for example: just client -PnoPowah')]
[group('gradle')]
client *flags:
    ./gradlew runClient "$@"

[doc('Start a dev dedicated server')]
[group('gradle')]
server *flags:
    ./gradlew runServer "$@"

[doc('Regenerate src/generated/resources')]
[group('gradle')]
data:
    ./gradlew runData

# The first run updates gradle-wrapper.properties with the old Gradle, and the second run lets the new Gradle rewrite gradlew and gradle-wrapper.jar to match it.
[doc('Upgrade the Gradle wrapper, for example: just gradle-update 9.8.2')]
[group('gradle')]
gradle-update version:
    ./gradlew wrapper --gradle-version "$1"
    ./gradlew wrapper --gradle-version "$1"

[doc('Run every pre-commit hook on every file, as CI does')]
[group('lint')]
lint: (require "prek")
    prek run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure

# The formatters exit 1 when they rewrite a file, so a second run decides the result: it passes when the first run fixed everything.
[doc('Format the Java, Markdown, YAML and JSON files in place')]
[group('lint')]
fmt: (require "prek")
    prek run --all-files pretty-format-java prettier || prek run --all-files pretty-format-java prettier

[doc('Lint the GitHub workflows with actrun and zizmor')]
[group('ci')]
ci-lint: (require "actrun" "zizmor")
    actrun lint
    zizmor --offline .github/workflows

# local-ci runs the jobs in Docker with GitHub's own runner, against the working tree including uncommitted changes.
[doc('Run the Build workflow locally in Docker, for example: just ci -p to pause on a failed step')]
[group('ci')]
ci *flags: (require "local-ci" "docker")
    @docker info >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "error: Docker is not running. Start Docker Desktop first." >&2; exit 1; }
    local-ci run --workflow .github/workflows/build.yml "$@"

[doc('Render the mod logo into docs/media/logo.png and src/main/resources/logo.png')]
[group('media')]
logo: (require "uv")
    uv run tools/render_logo.py

[doc('Compress PNG files in place, for example: just compress docs/media/*.png')]
[group('media')]
compress +files: (require "pngquant" "oxipng")
    pngquant --quality=80-95 --speed 1 --strip --force --ext .png "$@"
    oxipng -o 4 --strip safe "$@"

[doc('Print the changelog notes for one release tag, for example: just changelog 26.1.2-0.1.0')]
[group('release')]
changelog version:
    @bash tools/changelog-section.sh "$1"

[doc('Check that the version in gradle.properties is ready to tag, then dry-run the publish to GitHub, CurseForge and Modrinth')]
[group('release')]
release-check:
    bash tools/check-release.sh "$(bash tools/release-version.sh)"
    DRY_RUN=1 GITHUB_TOKEN=REDACTED ./gradlew publishMods

# Developing Modular Planters

## Setup

- JDK 25 on your `PATH`. Gradle 9.8.2 starts with JDK 17 or newer through the wrapper (`./gradlew`), and the build compiles with JDK 25, which Gradle can also download through the Foojay toolchain resolver. The Java formatter hook runs the `java` on your `PATH` and reads the code with that JDK's compiler, so it needs JDK 25.
- [just](https://just.systems) for the commands below and [prek](https://prek.j178.dev) for the pre-commit hooks: `brew install just prek`. Run `prek install` once in your clone. After that, each commit formats Java with google-java-format and Markdown, YAML and JSON with Prettier, then checks the workflows and shell scripts.
- Optional, for redrawing the logo with `just logo`: [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) (`brew install uv`). For compressing screenshots with `just compress`: `brew install pngquant oxipng`.
- Optional, for testing the GitHub workflows before pushing: Docker, `brew install zizmor`, and `bun add -g @mizchi/actrun run-local-ci`. `just ci` runs the Build workflow in Docker and `just ci-lint` lints the workflows.
- An IDE is optional. IntelliJ IDEA imports the project from `build.gradle`, and the `idea` plugin downloads sources and javadoc for Minecraft and NeoForge. `.editorconfig` sets Java to 2-space indents and 100 columns, matching google-java-format.

The first build downloads Minecraft, NeoForge and the dev mods, so it takes a few minutes.

## Commands

Run `just` to list the recipes. Each one wraps a Gradle task or a script in `tools/`, so `./gradlew runClient` and the rest still work without just.

| Command                        | What it does                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `just build`                   | Compiles, runs the unit tests and builds the jar into `build/libs/`                                       |
| `just test`                    | Runs the unit tests in `src/test`                                                                         |
| `just gametest`                | Starts a headless server that runs the in-game tests in `src/main/java/.../gametest` and exits            |
| `just check`                   | Runs the unit tests, then the in-game tests with every dev mod, with `-PnoAe2` and with `-PnoAppliedFlux` |
| `just client`                  | Starts a dev client with the mod and the dev mods below                                                   |
| `just server`                  | Starts a dev dedicated server with no GUI                                                                 |
| `just data`                    | Regenerates `src/generated/resources` (recipes, loot tables, lang, models)                                |
| `just gradle-update <version>` | Upgrades the Gradle wrapper to that version                                                               |
| `just lint`                    | Runs every pre-commit hook on every file                                                                  |
| `just fmt`                     | Formats the Java, Markdown, YAML and JSON files in place                                                  |
| `just ci-lint`                 | Lints the GitHub workflows with actrun and zizmor                                                         |
| `just ci`                      | Runs the Build workflow locally in Docker with local-ci, uncommitted changes included                     |
| `just logo`                    | Redraws the logo from the block textures                                                                  |
| `just compress <files>`        | Compresses PNG screenshots with pngquant and oxipng                                                       |
| `just changelog <tag>`         | Prints the changelog notes for one release                                                                |
| `just release-check`           | Checks that the version is ready to tag, then dry-runs the publish                                        |

Run `just check` and `just lint` before opening a pull request. After changing anything in `datagen`, also run `just data` and commit the result. The Build workflow runs all of these on every push and pull request, and fails if `runData` would change `src/generated`.

## Where things live

- `src/main/java`: the mod. The `gametest` and `datagen` packages are left out of the jar.
- `src/generated/resources`: output of `runData`. It is committed, so run `runData` and commit the result after changing anything in `datagen`.
- `wiki/`: the guide's pages. `processResources` copies them into the jar, where Oracle Index reads them as a book.
- `docs/description.md` and `docs/media/`: the CurseForge and Modrinth page and its images. World shots are JPEG. Screenshots of screens are PNG, compressed with `just compress <files>`, which runs `pngquant` and then `oxipng` (`brew install pngquant oxipng`). The logo PNGs are left as `tools/render_logo.py` writes them.
- `tools/changelog-section.sh`, `tools/check-release.sh` and `tools/release-version.sh`: the release checks that `just release-check` and the Release workflow run.
- `.github/workflows/`: `build.yml` runs `checks.yml` on every push and pull request, and `release.yml` runs it on a release tag before publishing.
- `tools/render_logo.py`: draws the logo from the block textures. Run `just logo` after changing a block texture, and commit both `docs/media/logo.png` and `src/main/resources/logo.png`.

## Dev mods

These are on the dev runtime (`runClient`, `runServer`, `runGameTestServer`) but not in the jar. Agritech: Evolved is the only required dependency. Each switch below leaves a mod out of a run, for example `just client -PnoAe2`.

| Mod                | Version       | Comes with                     | Switch                                     |
| ------------------ | ------------- | ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------ |
| Agritech: Evolved  | 2.2.0.6       |                                | required                                   |
| Jade               | 26.1.12       |                                | `-PnoJade`                                 |
| AE2                | 26.1.13-beta  | GuideME 26.1.15-beta           | `-PnoAe2`                                  |
| Applied Flux       | 26.1-1.0.2    | Glodium 26.1-1.2               | `-PnoAppliedFlux`, also off with `-PnoAe2` |
| Powah              | 7.0.4-alpha   | Cloth Config 26.1.154, GuideME | `-PnoPowah`                                |
| Oracle Index       | 2.0.0         | Architectury 20.1.17           | `-PnoOracleIndex`                          |
| Logistics Networks | 26.1.2-1.13.0 |                                | `-PnoLogisticsNetworks`                    |

The mod has code only for Jade, AE2 and Applied Flux. Powah is there for its fast FE source and cables. Oracle Index shows the guide, and Logistics Networks lets you test a node on the core. Most versions match the ones the All the Mods 11 modpack runs. Applied Flux isn't in that pack, and its AE2 build can differ.

## Releasing

A release tag is `<minecraft_version>-<mod_version>`, for example `26.1.2-0.1.0` or `26.3-0.2.0`. Pushing one runs the Release workflow. It checks the tag and runs the same checks as every push. Then it makes a GitHub release with the jar those checks built, and after that uploads the same jar to CurseForge and Modrinth.

1. Set `mod_version` in `gradle.properties` to three numbers, such as `0.2.0`. A `-alpha` or `-beta` suffix, such as `0.2.0-beta`, publishes an alpha or a beta. Without one it is a full release.
2. Add a `## <tag>` section to the top of `CHANGELOG.md`, below the intro line. Its notes become the release notes on all three sites.
3. Run `just release-check`. It builds the tag from `gradle.properties`, fails if the tag has the wrong format or the changelog has no notes for it, then dry-runs the publish.
4. Commit, then run `git tag <tag> && git push origin main <tag>`.

The workflow reads the repository secrets `CURSEFORGE_API_KEY` and `MODRINTH_API_KEY`, and the project ids `curseforge_project_id` and `modrinth_project_id` in `gradle.properties`. An empty id skips that site, and the run logs a notice saying so. The GitHub release uses the workflow's own token.

If an upload fails, for example because a site is down, use "Re-run failed jobs" on that workflow run. A fix that needs a code change is released as a new version with a new tag. A tag that was pushed is never moved.

## Screenshots with Structure Lab

`-PstructureLabJar=<path to jar>` adds Structure Lab to a dev run. It places a structure file in a flat world and saves screenshots from set camera angles, which is how the world shots in `docs/media/` were taken. It is a local build that isn't published, so leave the switch out unless you have the jar. It needs a world created with the "Structure Lab" world type.

# GameTests run every optional-mod variant in CI

Both the Build and Release workflows run the GameTests four times: with every dev mod, with `-PnoAe2`, with `-PnoAppliedFlux` and with `-PnoJade`. Without the variants, a crash for players who lack AE2, Applied Flux or Jade would never fail a test, because the dev runtime includes all three. It costs extra minutes per run, and `just check` runs the same four.

Jade was added as the fourth variant on 2026-11-06. Before that, CI skipped it even though the Jade plan required every GameTest to pass with `-PnoJade`.

# Handoff: ModularPlanters, tooling walkthrough paused, agent docs refactored

Written 2026-11-05, updated 2026-11-06. Continue in `~/DEV/git_repos/minecraft-mods/ModularPlanters` (NeoForge 26.1.2, `neo_version` 26.1.2.116). This replaces `~/tmp/2026-11-04-modularplanters-handoff/modularplanters-handoff-2026-11-04.md`, which is still the source for the Step 2 details listed below.

This file lives in `docs/superpowers/handoffs/`, which `.gitignore` excludes (`/docs/superpowers/`). The repo is public and pushes Entire session logs, so keep this file out of git.

## State

Uncommitted changes in the repo, all from the agent docs refactor below. Nothing was committed or pushed.

- Modified: `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`.
- New: `docs/agents/` with `verifying.md`, `optional-mods.md`, `gametests.md`, `docs-and-wiki.md`, `build-and-tooling.md`.
- Untracked and not made by this session: `.agents/` (a copy of the `minecraft-modding` skill) and `.codex/` (`config.toml`, `hooks.json`). They appeared in `git status` on 2026-11-06 and their origin is not established. Ask the user before touching, ignoring or adding them.

Outside the repo: `~/.config/papercuts.md` (two entries) and the Claude memory files.

The user removed `just-mcp`, so its connection failure is closed. Recall capture is paused for this repo (`.recall/.capture-paused`), and `history.md` stops on 2026-10-31, so `/recall:save` was not run.

## Step 1 result (tooling walkthrough)

- The `minecraft-modding` MCP is connected with 41 tools. `bunx` is 1.4.4 and Node is 26.13.0.
- Vanilla lookups against 26.1.2 work. NeoForge, FML and AE2 lookups need the targets in the table below.
- `neoforge-mod-workflow` and the repo verification rules were compared. CI's GameTest matrix (none, `-PnoAe2`, `-PnoAppliedFlux`) matches `just check`.

## Agent docs refactor (progressive disclosure), done 2026-11-06

Prompt: split the root agent file into essentials plus linked topic files, find contradictions, flag deletions.

Decisions from the user:

- `AGENTS.md` is the canonical root. `CLAUDE.md` is now the Entire block plus `@AGENTS.md`. Codex and other agents read the same rules as Claude Code.
- The datagen rule no longer says "commit the result". It says to leave the regenerated files for the owner to commit. The old wording contradicted the user's no-commit rule.

Result:

- `AGENTS.md` keeps the Entire block, the project description, the public-repo warning, five every-task rules, and links to the five topic files.
- Every rule from the old `CLAUDE.md` is still present (checked by searching for a key phrase from each line). Nothing was deleted.
- `prek run --files` passed, including Prettier, with no rewrites.
- `ProjectDocsTest` scans a fixed list of docs that does not include `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` or `docs/agents/`, so the new links cannot break `just test`. `just test` was not run.

Not resolved:

- Both `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` import `.entire/agent-guide.md`, because `entire` manages the block in each file. Whether Claude Code loads that 100-line file twice is not verified. If a session shows it twice, drop the `@.entire/agent-guide.md` line from one block and check that `entire` does not restore it.
- `.entire/agent-guide.md` (managed by `entire`, so not edited) and Graph's own output tell the agent to run `./gradlew test`. The repo rule is `just check` and `just lint`. Not a hard conflict, since `just check` includes the unit tests, but the two differ.
- Flagged for trimming, not changed: `.entire/agent-guide.md` repeats the Graph-then-Brain obligation in several places, and has vague lines such as "Prefer precise queries and line ranges, but never trade resolution for fewer turns" and "make the smallest complete change". It is regenerated by `entire`, so trimming means changing `entire` settings or accepting it.
- No line in the old `CLAUDE.md` was redundant, vague or obvious enough to delete. `just check` and `just lint` also appear in `DEVELOPMENT.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md`, which are for human contributors and stay.
- Personal workflow preferences (end-of-slice `just check`, no rebuild between slices) are not in the checked-in files, because the repo is public. They live in the `verification-cadence` memory.

Keep the skill generic, because it applies to every mod repo. `analyze-mod-jar` and `search-mod-source`, which the skill already names, are still untested on the AE2 jar.

### 2. Verification after Java changes

Run `just check` and `just lint` at the end of each slice, and otherwise do not rebuild. This settles the conflict between the workflow's `./gradlew build` and the global "don't rebuild unless asked". `just check` does not build the jar; CI still does.

# Codebase Design

Design **deep modules**: a lot of behaviour behind a small interface, placed at a clean seam, testable through that interface. Use this language and these principles wherever code is being designed or restructured. The aim is leverage for callers, locality for maintainers, and testability for everyone.

## Glossary

Use these terms exactly: don't substitute "component," "service," "API," or "boundary." Consistent language is the whole point.

**Module**: anything with an interface and an implementation. Deliberately scale-agnostic: a function, class, package, or tier-spanning slice. _Avoid_: unit, component, service.

**Interface**: everything a caller must know to use the module correctly: the type signature, but also invariants, ordering constraints, error modes, required configuration, and performance characteristics. _Avoid_: API, signature (too narrow, they refer only to the type-level surface).

**Implementation**: what's inside a module, its body of code. Distinct from **Adapter**: a thing can be a small adapter with a large implementation (a Postgres repo) or a large adapter with a small implementation (an in-memory fake). Reach for "adapter" when the seam is the topic; "implementation" otherwise.

**Depth**: leverage at the interface. The amount of behaviour a caller (or test) can exercise per unit of interface they have to learn. A module is **deep** when a large amount of behaviour sits behind a small interface, **shallow** when the interface is nearly as complex as the implementation.

**Seam** _(Michael Feathers)_: a place where you can alter behaviour without editing in that place; the *location* at which a module's interface lives. Where to put the seam is its own design decision, distinct from what goes behind it. _Avoid_: boundary (overloaded with DDD's bounded context).

**Adapter**: a concrete thing that satisfies an interface at a seam. Describes *role* (what slot it fills), not substance (what's inside).

**Leverage**: what callers get from depth. More capability per unit of interface they learn. One implementation pays back across N call sites and M tests.

**Locality**: what maintainers get from depth. Change, bugs, knowledge, and verification concentrate in one place rather than spreading across callers. Fix once, fixed everywhere.

## Deep vs shallow

**Deep module** = small interface + lots of implementation:

```
┌─────────────────────┐
│   Small Interface   │  ← Few methods, simple params
├─────────────────────┤
│                     │
│  Deep Implementation│  ← Complex logic hidden
│                     │
└─────────────────────┘
```

**Shallow module** = large interface + little implementation (avoid):

```
┌─────────────────────────────────┐
│       Large Interface           │  ← Many methods, complex params
├─────────────────────────────────┤
│  Thin Implementation            │  ← Just passes through
└─────────────────────────────────┘
```

When designing an interface, ask:

- Can I reduce the number of methods?
- Can I simplify the parameters?
- Can I hide more complexity inside?

## Principles

- **Depth is a property of the interface, not the implementation.** A deep module can be internally composed of small, mockable, swappable parts; they just aren't part of the interface. A module can have **internal seams** (private to its implementation, used by its own tests) as well as the **external seam** at its interface.
- **The deletion test.** Imagine deleting the module. If complexity vanishes, it was a pass-through. If complexity reappears across N callers, it was earning its keep.
- **The interface is the test surface.** Callers and tests cross the same seam. If you want to test *past* the interface, the module is probably the wrong shape.
- **One adapter means a hypothetical seam. Two adapters means a real one.** Don't introduce a seam unless something actually varies across it.

## Designing for testability

Good interfaces make testing natural:

1. **Accept dependencies, don't create them.**

   ```typescript
   // Testable
   function processOrder(order, paymentGateway) {}

   // Hard to test
   function processOrder(order) {
     const gateway = new StripeGateway();
   }
   ```

2. **Return results, don't produce side effects.**

   ```typescript
   // Testable
   function calculateDiscount(cart): Discount {}

   // Hard to test
   function applyDiscount(cart): void {
     cart.total -= discount;
   }
   ```

3. **Small surface area.** Fewer methods = fewer tests needed. Fewer params = simpler test setup.

## Relationships

- A **Module** has exactly one **Interface** (the surface it presents to callers and tests).
- **Depth** is a property of a **Module**, measured against its **Interface**.
- A **Seam** is where a **Module**'s **Interface** lives.
- An **Adapter** sits at a **Seam** and satisfies the **Interface**.
- **Depth** produces **Leverage** for callers and **Locality** for maintainers.

## Rejected framings

- **Depth as ratio of implementation-lines to interface-lines** (Ousterhout): rewards padding the implementation. We use depth-as-leverage instead.
- **"Interface" as the TypeScript `interface` keyword or a class's public methods**: too narrow: interface here includes every fact a caller must know.
- **"Boundary"**: overloaded with DDD's bounded context. Say **seam** or **interface**.

## Going deeper

- **Deepening a cluster given its dependencies**, see [DEEPENING.md](DEEPENING.md): dependency categories, seam discipline, and replace-don't-layer testing.
- **Exploring alternative interfaces**, see [DESIGN-IT-TWICE.md](DESIGN-IT-TWICE.md): spin up parallel sub-agents to design the interface several radically different ways, then compare on depth, locality, and seam placement.

# Deepening

How to deepen a cluster of shallow modules safely, given its dependencies. Assumes the vocabulary in [SKILL.md](SKILL.md): **module**, **interface**, **seam**, **adapter**.

## Dependency categories

When assessing a candidate for deepening, classify its dependencies. The category determines how the deepened module is tested across its seam.

### 1. In-process

Pure computation, in-memory state, no I/O. Always deepenable: merge the modules and test through the new interface directly. No adapter needed.

### 2. Local-substitutable

Dependencies that have local test stand-ins (PGLite for Postgres, in-memory filesystem). Deepenable if the stand-in exists. The deepened module is tested with the stand-in running in the test suite. The seam is internal; no port at the module's external interface.

### 3. Remote but owned (Ports & Adapters)

Your own services across a network boundary (microservices, internal APIs). Define a **port** (interface) at the seam. The deep module owns the logic; the transport is injected as an **adapter**. Tests use an in-memory adapter. Production uses an HTTP/gRPC/queue adapter.

Recommendation shape: *"Define a port at the seam, implement an HTTP adapter for production and an in-memory adapter for testing, so the logic sits in one deep module even though it's deployed across a network."*

### 4. True external (Mock)

# Deepening

How to deepen a cluster of shallow modules safely, given its dependencies. Assumes the vocabulary in [SKILL.md](SKILL.md): **module**, **interface**, **seam**, **adapter**.

## Dependency categories

When assessing a candidate for deepening, classify its dependencies. The category determines how the deepened module is tested across its seam.

### 1. In-process

Pure computation, in-memory state, no I/O. Always deepenable: merge the modules and test through the new interface directly. No adapter needed.

### 2. Local-substitutable

Dependencies that have local test stand-ins (PGLite for Postgres, in-memory filesystem). Deepenable if the stand-in exists. The deepened module is tested with the stand-in running in the test suite. The seam is internal; no port at the module's external interface.

### 3. Remote but owned (Ports & Adapters)

Your own services across a network boundary (microservices, internal APIs). Define a **port** (interface) at the seam. The deep module owns the logic; the transport is injected as an **adapter**. Tests use an in-memory adapter. Production uses an HTTP/gRPC/queue adapter.

Recommendation shape: *"Define a port at the seam, implement an HTTP adapter for production and an in-memory adapter for testing, so the logic sits in one deep module even though it's deployed across a network."*

### 4. True external (Mock)

## Testing strategy: replace, don't layer

- Old unit tests on shallow modules become waste once tests at the deepened module's interface exist; delete them.
- Write new tests at the deepened module's interface. The **interface is the test surface**.
- Tests assert on observable outcomes through the interface, not internal state.

content.text:
Three deepening candidates, plus what I'd leave alone. These are proposals only, and I changed no code. They use the skill's terms (module, interface, seam, depth) and the project's glossary and ADRs.

The code is already deep where it matters. `logic/` (ADR 0006) has real seams, and `StructureScanner` is the model: neighbors, part type and cap are injected, and plain JUnit tests it. The shallow spots are where the Core and a planter meet the world.

## A. Core resources as one module
**Files:** `blockentity/CoreBlockEntity.java`, `multiblock/DoorwayHandlers.java`, `menu/CoreMenu.java`, `menu/PlanterMenu.java`

- **Problem:** the Core holds six nullable fields (multiblock, power, fertilizer, outputs, me, items) and nine getters. Callers null-check one at a time.
  - **Reset in three places:** the same five-field reset appears in the scan's waiting branch (`:174-178`), in `buildPools` (`:214-219`) and in the initial state.
  - **Repeated null checks:** `CoreMenu.buildTable` repeats `core.power() == null ? 0 : …` four times (`:93-98`).
  - **Pass-throughs:** `DoorwayHandlers.energy(core)` and `items(core)` are one-liners that pass straight through.
  - **Duplicated rule:** the check "this Modular Planter Block belongs to this Core's formed multiblock" is written twice, in `CoreMenu.java:138-142` and `PlanterMenu.java:302-306`. It is the server-side check for client requests.
- **Deletion test:** deleting `DoorwayHandlers.energy/items(core)` loses nothing. Deleting the null handling just moves it into every caller.
- **Direction:** one nullable "what the Core holds while formed" module that owns the pools, the Doorway and the membership check, and answers totals directly.
  - **Core interface:** it shrinks to the scan result plus that module.
  - **ADR 0009:** while waiting for chunks, the module is absent, as the pools are today.
- **Seam:** internal, no new adapter. **Dependencies:** in-process.
- **Benefit:** locality for the authorization check, and fewer places the GameTests reach into Core internals (`StructureTests` alone calls `multiblock()` or `lastScan()` 13 times).
- **Risk:** low to medium.

## B. The ME move as one conserving operation
**Files:** `multiblock/OutputSink.java`, `multiblock/FertilizerPool.java`, `multiblock/PowerPool.java`, `multiblock/MeLink.java`

- **Problem:** `MeLink` has hidden rules in its comment (`MeLink.java:5-7`): no transaction open during an ME call, at most the amount asked, and a simulation changes nothing. Each caller re-implements the dance that follows from them:
  - **Move-out dance:** `moveExportsInto` (`OutputSink.java:103-149`) simulates, extracts in one transaction, offers to ME, then puts the refused part back in a second transaction.
  - **Pull-in dance:** `topUpFrom` (`FertilizerPool.java:112-154`) measures room, extracts from ME, then inserts.
  - **Last-resort drop loops:** both end with a near-identical "drop what can't be returned" loop.
  - **Rule held by callers:** the ME-transaction rule lives in the callers' discipline, not in one place.
- **Direction:** one module that moves a resource between a storage slot and ME, with the no-transaction rule and the drop fallback inside it.
  - **Callers:** the pools call it and no longer know about transactions.
  - **MeLink:** it stays the seam.
- **Seam:** `MeLink` already has two adapters, `MeBlockEntity` and `gametest/FakeMeLink`, so it is real (the skill's two-adapter rule). **Dependencies:** true external (AE2), reached through that seam.
- **Benefit:** the conservation guarantee ("never void or duplicate") is tested in one place. `MeLinkTests` already covers the cases and would move to the new interface.
- **Risk:** medium. Item loss would be the failure mode.

## C. The planter growth tick out of the block entity
**Files:** `blockentity/PlanterBlockEntity.java` (`tickFromCore` `:142-248`, `harvest` `:287-336`), `multiblock/TickContext.java`

- **Problem:** the decisions sit in a 438-line block entity beside saving, drops and ACTIVE-texture logic.
  - **Already extracted:** the math, in `PlanterTicker`, `Coverage`, `Grouping`, `GrowthMath` and `ClocheYield`.
  - **Still in the block entity:** the sequencing, which is where the Advanced Planter equivalence can break.
  - **Harvest order:** pre-harvest event, roll drops, round, post-harvest event, kept-fraction extras, insert, then consume fertilizer. ATE's events and `NeoForge.EVENT_BUS` are called inline.
  - **Test coverage:** only GameTests cover it. The unit-test reference model (`ReferenceAdvancedPlanter`) covers growth time and power only, not harvest order.
- **Direction:** a planter-tick module that takes the planter state and injected collaborators (power, fertilizer budget, outputs, the events) and returns an outcome. The block entity applies the outcome and saves.
- **Seam:** `TickContext` is the start of one. Production (ATE and NeoForge) and a test fake would be two adapters.
- **Constraint (ADR 0006):** `logic/` allows no Minecraft imports, so it would need to be generic over the stack type like `SeedBin<S>`, or live outside `logic/`.
- **Dependencies:** in-process plus true external (ATE events and recipes).
- **Benefit:** the harvest-order invariants would get plain JUnit tests.
- **Risk:** high. It touches the mod's core promise, so it needs equivalence tests first (`tdd`).

## Leave alone
- **`FertilizerBlockEntity` and `ExportBlockEntity`:** near-duplicates, but plan 2 ruled they stay separate under your repetition rule.
- **A port for ATE's `FertilizerData`:** it leaks past `AteBridge` into `FertilizerPool` and the planter, but there is one adapter, so a seam would be indirection.
- **The menus and screens:** shallow because NeoForge's menu glue is. I see no leverage there.

## Order
I'd go A, then B, then C. A is low-risk and narrows what the tests reach into. B reuses the fakes you already have. C is the biggest payoff but should wait until A and B have shrunk the surface it sits on.

input.prompt:
Design-only task. Do NOT edit, create or delete any file, and do not run builds or tests. Read code with Read/rg only.

Repo: /Users/sweetjp/DEV/git_repos/minecraft-mods/ModularPlanters (NeoForge 26.1.2, Java 25 mod). Source root: src/main/java/io/github/julianperge/modular_planters/ (call it J/). Read GLOSSARY.md and docs/adr/0005-*.md, 0006-*.md, 0009-*.md first.

VOCABULARY. Use these terms exactly, and do not say "component", "service", "API" or "boundary":
- module: anything with an interface and an implementation. interface: everything a caller must know (signatures, invariants, ordering, error modes, config). implementation: what is inside. depth: leverage at the interface (much behaviour behind a small interface). seam: where a module's interface lives. adapter: a thing that satisfies an interface at a seam. leverage: what callers get from depth. locality: what maintainers get (changes and bugs concentrate in one place).
- Deletion test: if you delete the module and the complexity reappears across N callers, it earns its keep; if it vanishes, it was a pass-through.
- One adapter means a hypothetical seam, two adapters means a real one. Do not add a seam nobody varies across.
- Project terms come from GLOSSARY.md (Core, Modular Planter Block, Doorway, Part, Multiblock, Formed, Problem, Power Block, Fertilizer Block, Export Block, ME Block). Use them.

THE PROBLEM. J/blockentity/CoreBlockEntity.java (258 lines) holds six nullable fields (multiblock, power, fertilizer, outputs, me, items) that are reset together in scan()'s WAITING_FOR_CHUNKS branch (around lines 171-178) and in buildPools (around lines 212-236), plus nine accessors (multiblock, power, fertilizer, outputs, items, meStatus, lastScan, allPartsLoaded, tickOffset). Callers null-check one pool at a time:
- J/menu/CoreMenu.java buildTable (lines ~71-100) builds the Core screen totals with four `core.power() == null ? 0 : ...` style checks; openPlanter (~132-148) checks that a planter position is in the formed multiblock.
- J/menu/PlanterMenu.java (~295-306) stillInCoreStructure repeats that membership check.
- J/multiblock/DoorwayHandlers.java: energy(core) and items(core) are one-line pass-throughs; items(fertilizer, outputs) builds the combined item handler.
- J/jade/JadeInfo.java reads only core.lastScan().
- CoreBlockEntity.tickPlanters (~62-86) uses power.refillFrom(me), builds a TickContext(level, random, AteBridge.numbers(), power, fertilizer.budget(), outputs), ticks each planter in multiblock.planters() order, and every ME_INTERVAL ticks calls outputs.moveExportsInto(me) and fertilizer.topUpFrom(me).
- The pools are J/multiblock/PowerPool.java, FertilizerPool.java, OutputSink.java, with LiveBlocks.java (removed-member tolerance via an onStale callback that makes the Core rescan).
- GameTests in J/gametest/ reach into the Core: StructureTests (multiblock(), lastScan() about 13 times), Ae2Tests (meStatus(), outputs().insert, fertilizer().available()), DoorwayTests, CoreScreenTests, JadeTests. Find where the Doorway capabilities are registered (rg DoorwayHandlers) and read that too.

THE CANDIDATE. Collapse the six nullable fields and their getters into one module that represents what the Core holds while formed: the pools, the Doorway and the planter-membership check, answering totals directly. Propose its interface and what happens to CoreBlockEntity's public surface and to DoorwayHandlers.

CONSTRAINTS EVERY DESIGN MUST SATISFY.
1. ADR 0009: while any part's chunk is unloaded (ScanResult problem WAITING_FOR_CHUNKS), the multiblock is kept, the pools are absent, planters keep progress, and nothing touches block entities in unloaded chunks.
2. ADR 0005: MeLink stays the AE2-free seam and its contract is unchanged (no transaction open during an ME call, return at most the amount asked, a simulated call changes nothing).
3. Pools must keep tolerating a member block entity being removed between scans.
4. Doorway capabilities (energy in via the Power Blocks, items: fertilizer insert plus outputs extract) are queried by pipes at any time. level.invalidateCapabilities(worldPosition) runs after a rebuild. While not formed the Core exposes nothing.
5. The remote-open authorization (a Modular Planter Block's position belongs to this Core's formed multiblock) must live in exactly one place and stay server-side.
6. Behaviour must not change. Existing GameTests should only need mechanical updates. J/jade/JadeInfo stays Jade-free.
7. Out of scope: PlanterBlockEntity.tickFromCore, the ME transfer dance in OutputSink/FertilizerPool, and merging FertilizerBlockEntity with ExportBlockEntity (the owner ruled those stay separate).
8. Project rule: repetition beats premature abstraction. Do not add a seam unless two adapters justify it.

YOUR DESIGN CONSTRAINT: Minimize the interface. Aim for 1 to 3 entry points at most on the module, and a similarly small surface left on CoreBlockEntity. Maximise leverage per entry point.

DELIVERABLE. Return it as your final message (markdown, about 600 words plus code). Sections:
1. Interface: Java signatures plus invariants, ordering constraints and error modes.
2. Usage: short examples for three callers: CoreBlockEntity.tickPlanters, CoreMenu.buildTable, and the remote-open membership check.
3. What the implementation hides behind the seam.
4. Dependency strategy: classify using in-process / local-substitutable / remote-but-owned / true-external, and name any adapters.
5. Trade-offs: where leverage is high, where it is thin. List which CoreBlockEntity accessors are kept or removed, and what happens to DoorwayHandlers.
No em dashes or other fancy unicode characters.

Repo: /Users/sweetjp/DEV/git_repos/minecraft-mods/ModularPlanters (NeoForge 26.1.2, Java 25 mod). Source root: src/main/java/io/github/julianperge/modular_planters/ (call it J/). Read GLOSSARY.md and docs/adr/0005-*.md, 0006-*.md, 0009-*.md first.

VOCABULARY. Use these terms exactly, and do not say "component", "service", "API" or "boundary":
- module: anything with an interface and an implementation. interface: everything a caller must know (signatures, invariants, ordering, error modes, config). implementation: what is inside. depth: leverage at the interface (much behaviour behind a small interface). seam: where a module's interface lives. adapter: a thing that satisfies an interface at a seam. leverage: what callers get from depth. locality: what maintainers get (changes and bugs concentrate in one place).
- Deletion test: if you delete the module and the complexity reappears across N callers, it earns its keep; if it vanishes, it was a pass-through.
- One adapter means a hypothetical seam, two adapters means a real one. Do not add a seam nobody varies across.
- Project terms come from GLOSSARY.md (Core, Modular Planter Block, Doorway, Part, Multiblock, Formed, Problem, Power Block, Fertilizer Block, Export Block, ME Block). Use them.

THE PROBLEM. J/blockentity/CoreBlockEntity.java (258 lines) holds six nullable fields (multiblock, power, fertilizer, outputs, me, items) that are reset together in scan()'s WAITING_FOR_CHUNKS branch (around lines 171-178) and in buildPools (around lines 212-236), plus nine accessors (multiblock, power, fertilizer, outputs, items, meStatus, lastScan, allPartsLoaded, tickOffset). Callers null-check one pool at a time:
- J/menu/CoreMenu.java buildTable (lines ~71-100) builds the Core screen totals with four `core.power() == null ? 0 : ...` style checks; openPlanter (~132-148) checks that a planter position is in the formed multiblock.
- J/menu/PlanterMenu.java (~295-306) stillInCoreStructure repeats that membership check.
- J/multiblock/DoorwayHandlers.java: energy(core) and items(core) are one-line pass-throughs; items(fertilizer, outputs) builds the combined item handler.
- J/jade/JadeInfo.java reads only core.lastScan().
- CoreBlockEntity.tickPlanters (~62-86) uses power.refillFrom(me), builds a TickContext(level, random, AteBridge.numbers(), power, fertilizer.budget(), outputs), ticks each planter in multiblock.planters() order, and every ME_INTERVAL ticks calls outputs.moveExportsInto(me) and fertilizer.topUpFrom(me).
- The pools are J/multiblock/PowerPool.java, FertilizerPool.java, OutputSink.java, with LiveBlocks.java (removed-member tolerance via an onStale callback that makes the Core rescan).
- GameTests in J/gametest/ reach into the Core: StructureTests (multiblock(), lastScan() about 13 times), Ae2Tests (meStatus(), outputs().insert, fertilizer().available()), DoorwayTests, CoreScreenTests, JadeTests. Find where the Doorway capabilities are registered (rg DoorwayHandlers) and read that too.

THE CANDIDATE. Collapse the six nullable fields and their getters into one module that represents what the Core holds while formed: the pools, the Doorway and the planter-membership check, answering totals directly. Propose its interface and what happens to CoreBlockEntity's public surface and to DoorwayHandlers.

CONSTRAINTS EVERY DESIGN MUST SATISFY.
1. ADR 0009: while any part's chunk is unloaded (ScanResult problem WAITING_FOR_CHUNKS), the multiblock is kept, the pools are absent, planters keep progress, and nothing touches block entities in unloaded chunks.
2. ADR 0005: MeLink stays the AE2-free seam and its contract is unchanged (no transaction open during an ME call, return at most the amount asked, a simulated call changes nothing).
3. Pools must keep tolerating a member block entity being removed between scans.
4. Doorway capabilities (energy in via the Power Blocks, items: fertilizer insert plus outputs extract) are queried by pipes at any time. level.invalidateCapabilities(worldPosition) runs after a rebuild. While not formed the Core exposes nothing.
5. The remote-open authorization (a Modular Planter Block's position belongs to this Core's formed multiblock) must live in exactly one place and stay server-side.
6. Behaviour must not change. Existing GameTests should only need mechanical updates. J/jade/JadeInfo stays Jade-free.
7. Out of scope: PlanterBlockEntity.tickFromCore, the ME transfer dance in OutputSink/FertilizerPool, and merging FertilizerBlockEntity with ExportBlockEntity (the owner ruled those stay separate).
8. Project rule: repetition beats premature abstraction. Do not add a seam unless two adapters justify it.

YOUR DESIGN CONSTRAINT: Maximise flexibility. Support many use cases and extension (for example Jade, screens, a future Part type, a second consumer of totals, new Doorway resources) without editing the module. You must still respect constraint 8, so say which flexibility is real (something varies today or has a named second user) and which is speculative and therefore left out.

DELIVERABLE. Return it as your final message (markdown, about 600 words plus code). Sections:
1. Interface: Java signatures plus invariants, ordering constraints and error modes.
2. Usage: short examples for three callers: CoreBlockEntity.tickPlanters, CoreMenu.buildTable, and the remote-open membership check.
3. What the implementation hides behind the seam.
4. Dependency strategy: classify using in-process / local-substitutable / remote-but-owned / true-external, and name any adapters.
5. Trade-offs: where leverage is high, where it is thin. List which CoreBlockEntity accessors are kept or removed, and what happens to DoorwayHandlers.
No em dashes or other fancy unicode characters.

  ## Design A: `FormedCore` (flexibility-maximising)
  
  One module, `multiblock/FormedCore`, replaces the six nullable fields. The Core holds `@Nullable FormedCore formed` plus the `lastScan` it already keeps. `lastScan` stays on the Core because it describes the scan, not the formed state, so `JadeInfo` is untouched.
  
  FormedCore has two states. RUNNING has live pools. PAUSED is the ADR 0009 state: the Multiblock is kept, the pools are absent. `Core.formed == null` means not formed, or no scan has seen the Core yet.
  
  ### 1. Interface
  
  ```java
  public final class FormedCore {
    /** Builds the pools from the block entities now in the level. Caller guarantees all parts are loaded. */
    public static FormedCore running(Level level, Multiblock mb, Runnable onStale);
  
    /** WAITING_FOR_CHUNKS: same Multiblock, pools dropped, nothing touches a block entity. */
    public FormedCore paused();
  
    public boolean isRunning();
    public List<BlockPos> planters();             // valid in both states (stopPlanters, Core screen rows)
    public boolean hasPlanter(BlockPos pos);      // false when PAUSED: the single remote-open rule
    public Totals totals();                       // Totals.ZERO when PAUSED
    public @Nullable EnergyHandler energyDoorway();                 // null when PAUSED
    public @Nullable ResourceHandler<ItemResource> itemDoorway();   // null when PAUSED
    public void tick(ServerLevel level, int tickOffset);            // no-op when PAUSED
    public OutputSink outputs();                  // gametests only (Ae2Tests inserts a harvest); main code never calls it
  
    public record Totals(long energy, long capacity, int fertilizer, int outputFillPercent, MeStatus me) {
      public static final Totals ZERO = new Totals(0, 0, 0, 0, MeStatus.NONE);
    }
  }
  ```
  
  Invariants and ordering:
  - `tick` does `power.refillFrom(me)` first, then builds the `TickContext`, then ticks planters in `multiblock.planters()` order, then on `ME_INTERVAL` calls `moveExportsInto` followed by `topUpFrom`. This is the current order.
  - `tick` re-checks `all()` loaded, so it never touches an unloaded chunk even if the Core's state is stale.
  - A removed ME link counts as absent, and `tick` calls `onStale`. A removed member calls `onStale` through `LiveBlocks`. Both make the Core set `dirty` and `poolsStale`.
  - `Totals` never throws. `meStatus` is `NONE` for a removed link.
  - The handlers are built once per `running(...)`, so the capability objects stay stable. They are safe to query from any thread-of-call that pipes use, and they return empty or zero once members are removed.
  - Server-side only. The class holds no client state.
  
  ### 2. Usage
  
  ```java
  // CoreBlockEntity.tickPlanters
  if (formed != null && level instanceof ServerLevel sl) formed.tick(sl, tickOffset());
  
  // CoreMenu.buildTable
  Totals t = core.totals();
  new CoreTablePayload.Totals(scan.formed(), scan.partCount(), cap, scan.problem(),
      Optional.ofNullable(scan.problemPos()), t.energy(), t.capacity(), draw,
      t.fertilizer(), t.outputFillPercent(), t.me());
  
  // CoreMenu.openPlanter and PlanterMenu.stillInCoreStructure (one rule)
  if (!core.hasPlanter(pos)) return;     // Core.hasPlanter = formed != null && formed.hasPlanter(pos)
  ```
  
  ### 3. What the implementation hides
  
  - The five pool fields, `MeLink` resolution and `isRemoved` checks.
  - The `onStale` wiring and the combined fertilizer-insert plus outputs-extract handler (including the `allLive()` rebuild fallback from `DoorwayHandlers.items(fertilizer, outputs)`).
  - The pause rules and the zero-totals rule.
  - The membership list. Today two menus repeat the test; after this, one place owns it.
  
  Scan stays in the Core and ends up calling only two things:
  - WAITING_FOR_CHUNKS: `formed = formed == null ? null : formed.paused()`.
  - Otherwise: `formed = result.formed() ? FormedCore.running(...) : null`, then `stopPlanters(previous.planters(), ...)`, then `invalidateCapabilities` (still in `scan()`).
  
  ### 4. Dependency strategy
  
  - **In-process:** the pools, `LiveBlocks`, `Multiblock`, the handlers.
  - **Local-substitutable:** the `Level` and block entities (the real thing is available in GameTests; there is no fake `Level`, and sqlite-style mocks are out).
  - **True-external, behind an existing seam:** AE2, reached only through `MeLink`. That has two adapters today (the AE2 one and the fake `MeLink` that ADR 0005 names), so it is a real seam, and its contract is unchanged. `FormedCore` takes no new seam.
  
  ### 5. Trade-offs
  
  **Flexibility that is real (kept):**
  - `Totals` is a record. The Core screen consumes it today, and Jade is a named second user: it can show totals by reading `core.totals()`, with no edit to `FormedCore`.
  - The PAUSED/RUNNING split varies today.
  - Adding a field to `Totals` touches one place.
  
  **Flexibility that is speculative (left out):**
  - A registry or `Map<Class, Pool>` for new Parts.
  - A pluggable Doorway resource list.
  - Listener or observer hooks.
  - An injected block-entity lookup. There is one adapter, `Level`, so it would be a hypothetical seam, and the repetition-over-abstraction rule says no.
  
  A new Part type or new Doorway resource edits `FormedCore` once, in one file. That is the locality payoff.
  
  **Core accessors:**
  - Removed: `multiblock`, `power`, `fertilizer`, `outputs`, `items`, `meStatus`, `allPartsLoaded`.
  - Kept: `lastScan`, `tickOffset`, `markDirty`.
  - Added: `totals()`, `planters()`, `hasPlanter(pos)`, `energyDoorway()`, `itemDoorway()`, and `formed()` for tests only.
  
  The count of public accessors barely drops. The gain is that callers no longer null-check pools one at a time.
  
  **`DoorwayHandlers`:** deleted. `energy(core)` and `items(core)` fail the deletion test because they are pass-throughs. The combining logic moves into `FormedCore`, and `MPBlockEntities` registers `(be, side) -> be.energyDoorway()` and `(be, side) -> be.itemDoorway()`.
  
  **Where leverage is high:** `buildTable`, both menus, and the pause rule, which is now stated once.
  
  **Where it is thin:** the two Doorway one-liners on the Core, and `outputs()` kept for tests.
  
  **GameTests:**
  - `StructureTests` replaces `multiblock()` with `formed().planters()`.
  - `Ae2Tests` uses `totals().fertilizer()` and `formed().outputs()`.
  - `lastScan()` and `meStatus()` map directly.
  
  No behaviour changes.

  public final class FormedCore {
    // Builds the pools, finds the ME link, builds the Doorway handlers. Call only when all parts are loaded.
    public static FormedCore running(Level level, Multiblock mb, Runnable onStale);
    // Keeps the Multiblock, holds no pools and no ME link (ADR 0009).
    public static FormedCore paused(Multiblock mb);
  
    // 1. Ticks every planter in Multiblock order. No-op when paused or when any part is unloaded.
    public void tick(ServerLevel level, long phase);
  
    // 2. Totals plus planter positions for the Core screen. Zeros and NONE when paused.
    public Totals totals();
    public record Totals(List<BlockPos> planters, long energyStored, long energyCapacity,

      public static final Totals EMPTY = /* empty list, zeros, MeStatus.NONE */;
    }
  
    // 3. The only remote-open authorization. False when paused.
    public boolean owns(BlockPos planter);

    public record Doorway(EnergyHandler energy, ResourceHandler<ItemResource> items) {}

  ```

Folding it into `totals()` would push the authorization back into callers and make `stillValid` compute sums every tick. The `planters` list in `Totals` includes the kept planters while paused, because the Core screen shows loaded planter rows during a wait today.
  
  Invariants, ordering and error modes:
  - `phase` is `gameTime + core.tickOffset()`. The ME interval check is `phase % ME_INTERVAL == 0`.
  - `onStale` fires when a pool or the ME link reports a removed member. It fires from `tick`, `totals` or a handler call, never from the factory. CoreBlockEntity points it at `markPoolsStale`, so the next scan rebuilds.
  - No method throws. Absent pools mean zeros, `false`, `null` or a no-op.
  - ME calls happen only inside `tick`, never inside Doorway handlers, so no transaction is open during an ME call. The `MeLink` contract is unchanged.

    public Totals totals();

                         int fertilizer, int outputFillPercent, MeStatus me) {
      public static final Totals EMPTY = /* empty list, zeros, MeStatus.NONE */;
    }
  
    // 3. The only remote-open authorization. False when paused.
    public boolean owns(BlockPos planter);
  
    // 4. Doorway for pipes. Null when paused.
    public @Nullable Doorway doorway();
    public record Doorway(EnergyHandler energy, ResourceHandler<ItemResource> items) {}
  }
  ```

The `planters` list in `Totals` includes the kept planters while paused, because the Core screen shows loaded planter rows during a wait today.

  - `phase` is `gameTime + core.tickOffset()`. The ME interval check is `phase % ME_INTERVAL == 0`.

lastPrompt: design its interface two or three ways and compare them, using the skill’s design-it-twice step.

content.text:
All three designs agree on the core move and differ on how wide the interface is. I recommend a hybrid, described at the end. The designs are on paper only: I changed no code, and none of them was compiled.

All three call the module `FormedCore`. It replaces the six nullable fields on `CoreBlockEntity`, deletes `DoorwayHandlers`, keeps `lastScan()` on the Core, and leaves `MeLink` unchanged. Each has a running state and a paused state, and the paused state is the ADR 0009 case: the multiblock is kept, the pools are absent.

## Design 1: minimal (four entry points)
- **Interface:** an immutable `FormedCore` with `tick`, `totals`, `owns(pos)` and `doorway`. The Core holds one nullable field.
- **Totals:** `Totals` includes the planter list, because the Core screen shows rows while the Core waits for chunks.
- **Cost:** it takes `outputs()` away from the GameTests. `Ae2Tests` inserts harvests through it at 8 sites, and the design says this needs a decision.
- **Caveat:** its agent did not read `PowerPool`, `FertilizerPool` or `OutputSink`, so the design is the least verified.
- **Callers:** they still write `core.formed() == null ? EMPTY : core.formed().totals()`, which moves the null check up one level instead of removing it.

## Design 2: flexible (about ten methods)
- **Interface:** `running(...)`, `paused()`, `isRunning()`, `planters()`, `hasPlanter`, `totals`, `energyDoorway`, `itemDoorway`, `tick`, plus a test-only `outputs()`.
- **Flexibility:** it names which flexibility is real and which it left out as speculative. A `Totals` record is real because Jade is a named second user. A part registry, pluggable Doorway resources and listener hooks were left out.
- **Weakness:** the interface is wide, and the accessor count barely drops.

## Design 3: common caller (`tickPlanters`)
- **Evidence:** the agent counted callers. GameTests dominate by call sites (`lastScan()` leads, 15 in tests and 6 in main). `tickPlanters` dominates by runtime, since it runs every tick for every Core.
- **Interface:** `tickPlanters` becomes one line. The Core keeps null-safe pass-throughs (`totals()`, `ownsPlanter()`, `energy()`, `items()`), so no caller null-checks `formed`.
- **Weakness:** `FormedCore` keeps `power()`, `fertilizer()`, `outputs()` and `multiblock()` for tests and the Core. That re-exposes the pools the module was meant to hide.

## Comparison
| | Depth | Locality | Seam placement |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Minimal | Deepest | Good, but null checks still sit in callers | Same for all three: one module owns the pools, and `MeLink` is the only seam |
| 2. Flexible | Middle | Good | |
| 3. Common caller | Thinnest, because of the test accessors | Best at the call sites | |

## Recommendation: hybrid
- **From design 1:** the immutable running/paused `FormedCore` with four entry points, which is the deepest option.
- **From design 3:** null-safe pass-throughs on the Core, so the null check lives in one place.
- **From design 2:** keep a single test-only `outputs()`. `Ae2Tests` needs it to insert harvests, and every other pool accessor goes away.
- **Doorway:** expose `energy()` and `items()` as two nullable methods, not a record, so the capability lambdas don't need a double null check.

Two risks:
- **Tests:** the Ae2 and Doorway GameTests are not purely mechanical updates. The `outputs()` hook is the one real decision, and it is yours.
- **Capability cache:** any holder of a `FormedCore` across ticks goes stale when it is replaced on rebuild. `invalidateCapabilities` should cover the only holder, but that needs a test.

I saved the summary in the handoff doc.

Should I adopt the hybrid and move on to `grilling`, which stress-tests it before any code? Or would you rather look at candidate B or C first?

Interview the user relentlessly until you reach a shared understanding. Map this as a **design tree**: every decision branches into the decisions that hang off it.

Work the tree in **rounds**. The **frontier** is every decision whose prerequisites are already settled: the questions you can ask _now_ without guessing at answers you haven't heard yet. Ask the whole frontier in one round: number each question and give your recommended answer. Then wait for the user's answers before the next round.

Format a round like so:

```
❓ **Q1** - **<question title>**: <question body, might be multiple paragraphs, including multiple choices>

➡️ <your recommended answer>

---

❓ **Q2** - **<question title>**: <question body, might be multiple paragraphs, including multiple choices>

➡️ <your recommended answer>
```

Word each question so "yes" accepts your recommended answer.

Each round the user answers reshapes the tree: settled decisions push the frontier outward and unblock questions that depended on them. Recompute the frontier and ask the next round. A question whose answer depends on another question still open in this round belongs to a _later_ round, not this one.

Finding _facts_ is your job, never the user's. When a frontier question needs a fact from the environment (filesystem, tools, etc.), dispatch a sub-agent to find it; don't ask the user for anything you could look up yourself. Don't block on it: a running exploration is an unsettled prerequisite, so only the questions downstream of it wait for the sub-agent to report; ask the rest of the frontier now. The _decisions_ are the user's: put each to them and wait.

The session is done when the frontier is empty: every branch of the design tree visited, nothing left silently assumed. Do not act on it until the user confirms you have reached a shared understanding.
