Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

1	# Domain Docs
2	
3	How the engineering skills should consume this repo's domain documentation when exploring the codebase.
4	
5	## Before exploring, read these
6	
7	- **`GLOSSARY.md`** at the repo root, or
8	- **`GLOSSARY-MAP.md`** at the repo root if it exists: it points at one `GLOSSARY.md` per context. Read each one relevant to the topic.
9	- **`docs/adr/`**: read ADRs that touch the area you're about to work in. In multi-context repos, also check `src/<context>/docs/adr/` for context-scoped decisions.
10	
11	If any of these files don't exist, **proceed silently**. Don't flag their absence; don't suggest creating them upfront. The `/domain-modeling` skill (reached via `/grill-with-docs` and `/improve-codebase-architecture`) creates them lazily when terms or decisions actually get resolved.
12	
13	## File structure
14	
15	Single-context repo (most repos):
16	
17	```
18	/
19	├── GLOSSARY.md
20	├── docs/adr/
21	│   ├── 0001-event-sourced-orders.md
22	│   └── 0002-postgres-for-write-model.md

32	└── src/

36	    └── billing/

42

48	
49	If your output contradicts an existing ADR, surface it explicitly rather than silently overriding:
50

- It destroys the second block and waits for the Core to build a new `LiveMultiblock`.
- After the rebuild, `totals().fertilizer()` is 10. Inserting 5 bone meal through the Core's item Doorway takes all 5, and the total becomes 15.

This was never red. The rebuild behaviour already existed, so the test is a characterization test that passed on its first run. The only way to see it fail would be to break the code on purpose. Say if you want me to do that.

The test asserts `core.live() != before`, so it depends on the rebuild creating a new instance. `just check` (all four variants) and `just lint` both passed.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/sweetjp/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.3.1/skills/productivity/writing-for-agents

Reference for writing any document an agent consumes: a skill, an `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md`, a doc reached by a pointer. The packaging differs; the writing does not: the same levers make each one predictable, since the agent takes the same _process_ every run rather than producing the same output.

When the document you're writing is a skill, read [`SKILL-MECHANICS.md`](SKILL-MECHANICS.md) for frontmatter, invocation choice, and router skills.

## Context pointers

A **context pointer** is a reference held in the agent's context that names some out-of-context material and encodes the condition for reaching it. A skill's description is one; a line in `AGENTS.md` naming a doc is the same object. The pointer's _wording_, not its target, decides when the agent reaches the material, and how reliably. A must-have target behind a weakly worded pointer is a variance bug: sharpen the wording first, and inline the material only if sharpening fails.

A pointer does two jobs: state what the material is, and list the **branches** that should trigger reaching it (a branch is a distinct case the document handles, so different runs take different paths through it). Every word of an always-loaded pointer costs on every turn, so it earns even harder pruning than the body:

- **Front-load the leading word**: the pointer is where it does its triggering work.
- **One trigger per branch.** Synonyms that rename a single branch are one branch written twice; collapse them and keep only genuinely distinct branches.
- **Cut identity the body already carries.**

## The two loads

Every document and pointer you add spends one of two budgets:

- **Context load** is the cost of always-loaded material on the agent's window: an `AGENTS.md` line, a skill description, anything sitting in context every turn, spending tokens and attention whether or not it fires.
- **Cognitive load** is the cost on the human: which documents exist and when to reach for each. The human is the index. Not a cost to minimise: it is the price of human agency; spend it where human judgement matters, remove it where it does not.

Material reached only through a pointer escapes context load at the price of the pointer's own line; material with no pointer at all rides entirely on cognitive load.

## Information hierarchy

A document is built from two content types: **steps** (the ordered actions the agent performs) and **reference** (definitions, rules, facts consulted on demand). The two mix freely: all steps (a recipe), all reference (a review's rules, this skill), or both. The core decision is where each piece sits on the **information hierarchy**, a ladder ranked by how immediately the agent needs the material:

1. **In-file step** is the primary tier: what the agent does, in order.
2. **In-file reference** is consulted on demand. Often a legitimately flat peer-set (every rule of a review on one rung), which is a fine arrangement, not a smell.
3. **Disclosed reference** is pushed out into a separate file, reached by a context pointer, loaded only when the pointer fires. Spans a sibling file in the same folder through fully external reference that lives anywhere and any document can point at.

Push too little down and the top bloats; push too much and you hide material the agent actually needs. That tension is the whole decision.

**Progressive disclosure** is the move down the ladder (out of the main file and behind a pointer) so the top stays legible. Not primarily a token optimisation: it is how the hierarchy is protected. Branching is the cleanest disclosure test: inline what every branch needs, and push behind a pointer what only some branches reach. When a document has steps, in-file reference that should be disclosed buries them and turns attending to them into a coin-flip: a variance lever, not just a legibility one.

**Co-location** is the within-file companion: where the ladder decides _how far down_ a piece sits, co-location decides _what sits beside it_ once there. Keep a concept's definition, rules, and caveats under one heading rather than scattered, so reading one part brings its neighbours with it. The test: the document should read like documentation written for the agent. Grouped material reads that way; scattered material does not. (Distinct from duplication: that repeats one meaning in two places; scattering fragments one meaning across many.)

**Sprawl** is the failure mode here: a document simply too long, even when every line is live and unique. Attention thins across the excess, and every extra line is one more to keep relevant. The cure is the ladder: disclose reference behind pointers, and split by branch or sequence so each path carries only what it needs.

## Steps and completion criteria

Every step ends on a **completion criterion**, the condition that tells the agent the work is done. Two properties make it a lever:

- **Clarity**: can the agent tell done from not-done? A vague bound ("understanding reached") invites **premature completion**: ending the step before it is genuinely done, attention slipping to _being done_. The visible steps still ahead (the **post-completion steps**) supply the pull; the criterion's clarity is the resistance. Defend in order: **sharpen the bound first** (local and cheap); only if it is irreducibly fuzzy _and_ you observe the rush, hide the later steps by splitting the sequence. Hiding only works across a real context boundary (a hand-off or a subagent dispatch; an inline call leaves the later steps in context and clears nothing).
- **Demand**: how much it requires. "Every modified model accounted for" forces thorough work where "produce a change list" does not. Demand drives **legwork** (the digging the agent does within the work, latent in the wording rather than written as its own step), and it is not step-bound: "every rule applied" binds a body of flat reference just as "every step done" binds a sequence, which is how an all-reference document still carries an exhaustiveness bar.

The strongest criteria are both checkable and exhaustive.

## When to split

Splitting one document into two spends one of the two loads, so split only when the cut earns it:

- **By sequence**: split a run of steps where the post-completion steps tempt the agent to rush the one in front of it. Keeping them out of view drives more legwork on the current task. Beware the reverse: merging sequences exposes each step's later steps to what follows, inviting premature completion.
- **By invocation**, skill-specific: see [`SKILL-MECHANICS.md`](SKILL-MECHANICS.md).

## Leading words

A **leading word** is a compact concept already living in the model's pretraining that the agent thinks with while running the document (_lesson_, _fog of war_, _tracer bullets_). Repeated as a token, never as a sentence, it accumulates a distributed definition and anchors a whole region of behaviour in the fewest tokens, by recruiting priors the model already holds. Coining your own works if you define it clearly, but a made-up word recruits no priors: you pay in definition tokens what a pretrained word gives free; reach for an existing word first.

It anchors twice. In the body, _execution_: the agent reaches for the same behaviour every time the word appears, and inside flat reference it focuses attention on a class of thing to look for. In a pointer, _invocation_: when the same word lives in your prompts, your docs, and your codebase, the agent links that shared language to the material and reaches it more reliably.

Hunt for opportunities to refactor with leading words. A triad spelled out at three sites, a pointer spending a sentence to gesture at one idea. Each is a passage begging to collapse into a single token:

- "fast, deterministic, low-overhead" → _tight_ (a _tight_ loop).
- "a loop you believe in" → _red_, turning a fuzzy gate into a binary observable state (the loop goes _red_ on the bug, or it doesn't).

You win twice: fewer tokens, and a sharper hook for the agent to hang its thinking on. Assume every document is carrying restatements that leading words retire. Go find them.

**Negation** is the failure mode beside this lever: steering by prohibition drags the forbidden behaviour into context and makes it _more_ available, not less. _Don't think of an elephant_, and the elephant is all there is; the negation is a weak modifier the strongly-activated concept overruns, so the ban half-reads as an instruction to do the thing. Prompt the **positive**: state the target behaviour ("write one-line comments") so the banned one is never spoken. A prohibition earns its place only as a hard guardrail you cannot phrase positively; even then, pair it with the positive target so attention lands on what to do.

## Pruning

- Keep each meaning in a **single source of truth**: one authoritative place, so changing the behaviour is a one-place edit. **Duplication** (the same meaning in more than one place) costs maintenance and tokens, and inflates a meaning's prominence on the ladder past its real rank. (The accidental inverse of a leading word, which repeats a token on purpose, never the meaning.)
- The **environment** is a source of truth too (`package.json` scripts, config files, the directory layout, `--help` output), and a document that restates it is a **cache**: a copy of a lookup, earning its load only when the lookup is expensive. Cache what the agent cannot find by looking: the unwritten convention, the reason behind a choice, the gotcha no config confesses. Leave the one-file, one-command lookups to the environment, where they cannot go stale.
- Check every line for **relevance**: does it still bear on what the document does? A line loses relevance by never bearing on the task (mere exposition, or a branch that should be disclosed) or by going stale as the behaviour or world it describes changes. Shorter documents are easier to keep relevant. Without a pruning discipline the default fate is **sediment**: stale layers that settle because adding feels safe and removing feels risky, until you must core down through them to find what is still live.
- Hunt **no-ops** sentence by sentence: an instruction the model already obeys by default pays load to say nothing. The test (does it change behaviour versus the default?) is model-relative, not reader-relative: two people disagreeing about a no-op disagree about the default, and settle it by running the document, not by debate. When a sentence fails, delete the whole sentence rather than trim words from it. The test also grades leading words: a word too weak to beat the default (_be thorough_ when the agent is already thorough-ish) is a no-op, and the fix is a stronger word (_relentless_), not a different technique.

=== verifying
# Verifying changes

- Run `just check` and `just lint`.
- After changing `datagen`, run `just data`. Leave the regenerated files in `src/generated/resources` for the owner to commit. The Build workflow fails if `runData` would change them.
- GameTests cannot prove that Jade tooltips or the Oracle Index book work. Jade swallows plugin exceptions and checks its provider rules only on a physical client, so ask the owner for an in-game check.
=== optional-mods
# Optional mods and the ME link

Agritech: Evolved is the only required dependency. DEVELOPMENT.md lists the `-Pno...` switches that leave a dev mod out of a run.

- The mod must load with any optional mod missing. AE2 classes stay in the `ae2` package behind `ModList.get().isLoaded("ae2")`, and generated data that references AE2 or `modular_planters:me` carries a `mod_loaded` condition.
- `MeLink` implementations return at most the requested amount, and a simulated call changes nothing. Callers subtract the result without clamping, so over-reporting voids items.
=== gametests
# GameTests

- `assert` does nothing in GameTests because the server JVM runs without `-ea`. Use `helper.fail(...)`.
- `makeMockPlayer(GameType.CREATIVE)` leaves `hasInfiniteMaterials()` false, so set `abilities.instabuild = true` as well.
- `GameTestHelper.assertValueEqual(actual, expected, msg)` prints its values swapped: "Expected X to be A: was B" means the actual value was A.
=== docs-and-wiki
# Docs, wiki and store pages

- `wiki/` pages are MDX, so a placeholder like `<problem>` parses as a JSX tag and breaks the page.
- ProjectDocsTest checks links against `git ls-files`, so a linked file must be tracked and match its exact case.
- `docs/description.md` loads its images from `main`, so push before pasting it into CurseForge or Modrinth.
=== build-and-tooling
# Build and tooling

- Keep `cache-provider: basic` on setup-gradle. The default provider accepts proprietary Terms of Use, and only the owner can agree to those.
- Hooks in `.claude/settings.json` call tools by name behind a `command -v` check, never by absolute path.
- `entire graph` misses calls through record accessors such as `ctx.outputs().insert(...)`, so check `TickContext` callers in source before refactoring.
- `./gradlew clean` wipes `build/moddev`, and rebuilding it needs the network.

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/sweetjp/.claude/skills/julian-voice

# Julian's Voice

Julian writes like a teammate typing between tasks: short, plain, first person, specific. Most messages are 1-3 sentences of 10-35 words. He goes long only to explain a cause or announce a change, and then he writes paragraphs, not lists.

## This skill overrides chat-style rules

Caveman mode, terse-output rules, and the "no hedging" rule in CLAUDE.md govern how Claude talks to Julian. They do not apply to drafts written as Julian. His real voice uses full sentences, articles, and softeners like "I think" and "Not sure if ...?". Keep them. If a humanizer pass runs afterwards, this skill wins on conflicts.

## Before drafting

Read the examples file for the context you are writing in. Match its length and shape before you match its words.

| Context | Examples file |
|---|---|
| Chat DM or channel | `examples/chat.md` |
| PR review comment or reply | `examples/pr-comments.md` |
| PR title, PR description, commit message | `examples/pr-and-commits.md` |
| GitHub issue or issue comment | `examples/issues.md` |

## After drafting

Once a draft is final and meant to be posted, log it so Julian's later edits can improve this skill. Pass the draft text on stdin:

```bash
uv run ~/.claude/skills/julian-voice/scripts/feedback.py draft --context <context> --target <target>
```

| Context | `--context` | `--target` |
|---|---|---|
| Chat | `chat` | server and channel, or DM partner |
| PR review comment | `pr-comment` | PR URL |
| PR description / title | `pr-description` / `pr-title` | PR URL |
| Commit message | `commit` | absolute path of the local repo |
| Issue comment / new issue | `issue-comment` / `issue` | issue URL, or repo URL for a new issue |

Log one entry per piece of text. A PR title and its description are two entries. When Julian asks to review voice feedback, follow `FEEDBACK.md` in this skill's directory.

## Shape by context

**Chat.** Median 19 words. Lowercase starts and no final period are normal. Casual words are normal: "y'all", "gonna", "cuz", "rq", "iirc", "lol". End with a `:shortcode:` emoji when one fits (`:+1:`, `:joy:`, `:shrug:`, `:facepalm:`). Greet only when opening a conversation or channel post: "Howdy", "Morning y'all,", "Hey team,". Links go on their own line with a one-line description. Times look like "1230 EST".

**PR review comment.** Median 16 words. Pick one of three forms:
- A bare fragment for trivial fixes: "lingering import", "Can be removed", "Use `pytest.approx` instead."
- A lowercase label: `nitpick:`, `suggestion:`, `question:`, followed by a direct sentence and its reason.
- A question for judgment calls: "Would it make sense to ...?", "Is there a way to ...?", "What do you think about ...?", followed by "Mostly asking since ...".

Put code after "something like this:" in an untagged fence. Identifiers go in backticks. Link docs as evidence.

**Replying to review.**
- Accepting: "Good catch, changed." / "Good point." / "Thanks for catching that." plus what you did.
- Your own mistake: "Whoops," / "Shoot," / "my bad" plus the fix in one clause.
- Changing your mind later: "Coming back to this, ..." or "The more I thought about it, ...".
- Pushing back: concede part first ("I agree, but ...", "True, and ..."), then the concrete reason. For a strong position use "I'm going to push against ... because ...".
- Approving: "LGTM, rebase your branch and then I'll approve :thumbsup:".

**PR title.** Check the repo's recent history with `git log` first. If the repo already follows its own format, such as `type(scope): subject` or a leading `(#123)` issue number, use that format. Otherwise the format is `type: subject`.
- **Types:** `feat`, `fix`, `ci`, `chore`, `doc`, `revert`, `test`. A breaking change is `feat!:`.
- **Subject:** a lowercase imperative clause with no trailing period: "feat: give the connector egress to its origins".
- **Joining items:** use ", " ("fix: cap workers at 50 jobs, raise root volume to 50GB, fix the Docker cleanup").
- **Why the title matters:** when the repo squash-merges, the title becomes the commit on the default branch.

The older styles (`KEY-N - Adding ...`, `NOREF - ...`) in `examples/pr-and-commits.md` are history. Use them only when Julian asks for that style.

**PR description.** Median 20 words. Open with the non-obvious fact, the reason, a link ("See <url>"), or "Also ...". The title already says what the PR does, so the description starts where the title stops. For several changes, use `- ` bullets starting with Added/Updated/Removed/Moved/Renamed, or "`identifier` updated from `X` to `Y`". Give each reason inline ("as", "since", "in favor of") or in a nested sub-bullet. Show proof with a short lead line: "Confirmed working here: <workflow run url>", a fenced error, or a captioned screenshot. End after the last fact. Headers appear only in long descriptions, and they name an area ("## Helm Related Changes").

**Commit message.** The subject follows the same format rule as the PR title: the repo's own format when it has one, otherwise `type: subject`. In someone else's repo, copy the owner's convention for the body too, judged from their recent commits in `git log`:
- **Owner writes subject-only commits:** write a subject only, such as `fix(quests): Dragon's Breath farming hint and Trinity Gem boss capture`.
- **Owner writes bodies:** wrap at 80 columns and walk the cause. Open with what is broken ("Without this patch applied, ..."), trace it through exact `Class#method` names, then say what "This patch ..." changes and what stays unaffected. `examples/pr-and-commits.md` has a full example.
- **Repo has no convention:** write one to three short sentences saying why, in his voice.

```
fix: publish releases with an image that has the gh cli

The release job was using an image without gh, so it failed before publishing.
```

**GitHub issue.** Start with "As an engineer, I want to ..." or a plain problem statement. Follow with evidence (error text, workflow run link). Then bold labels on their own lines: `**TASKS:**`, `**AC:**`, `**QA:**`, plus `**REPOS:**` or `**References:**` when useful. Tasks name exact variables, paths, and values. AC are observable outcomes. Small issues can be one or two lines.

**Issue comment.** Open with @mentions when addressing people, with the question on the same line or the next. Status updates are past tense and carry proof: "Deployed to dev: <url>", "Confirmed working in dev after rerunning the previously failed run." Close issues with "Marking as won't do, as ..." or "Implemented with <link>". Put any "cc @Name" line last. No "!" and no emoji.

## Habits across contexts

- **Requests:** "When you get a chance, do you mind ...?" plus why. "Please" is rare.
- **Hedges:** one per message, placed before the claim, followed by the reason. Use "I think", "Not sure if ...?", "I believe", "probably", "imo", or "(could be wrong on this)".
- **Questions:** state your own guess and end with "right?" or "correct?". Ask what someone meant before assuming: "Not sure I follow what you mean by that?"
- **Causes:** "The issue is that ...". Walk the chain step by step, use exact identifiers, and paste the error line.
- **Linkers:** "That way ...", "On top of that, ...", "instead of", "for some reason", "e.g.", "~" for approximate numbers ("~3-5 minutes").
- **Emphasis:** `_underscore_` italics or one word in CAPS ("MUCH", "NOT"). Bold appears only as issue section labels.
- **Humor:** dry, aimed at himself or at the tools, never at the reviewer.

## Swap these for his forms

| Instead of | He writes |
|---|---|
| Em dash, en dash, or semicolon | A comma, a period, or a new sentence |
| "Additionally" / "Furthermore" | "Also" / "On top of that," |
| "i.e." | "e.g." or "for example" |
| "Great question!" / "Thanks for the thorough review!" | Get straight to the answer |
| "Hope this helps" / "Let me know your thoughts!" | Stop after the last fact. Use "Let me know" only when tied to a specific action. |
| `## Summary` / `## Changes` / `**Label:** value` in a PR | Plain bullets or 1-3 sentences |
| Turning a conversational message into a bullet list | Prose. Lists only for truly parallel items. |
| Placeholder sample data (`device-1`) | Realistic values (UUIDs, real timestamps) |
| Literal emoji glyphs | `:shortcode:` |
| "You're absolutely right" | "You are correct," / "Yep you're right." |
| Restating the PR title as the first line | The non-obvious fact, reason, or link |

## Quick prompt

Short, plain, first person. One to three sentences unless explaining a cause. Use the format of the context: lowercase labels in reviews, past-tense proof in issues, -ing titles, commits in the repo owner's format. Soften with "I think" or "Not sure if ...?" and give the reason. Back claims with a link. No em dashes, semicolons, headers in comments, bold outside issue labels, sign-offs, or recaps. Read the matching examples file first.

# universal-modder compared with the ModularPlanters Minecraft tooling

Researched 2026-11-05 against `rehan-remade/universal-modder` at commit `9811709`. Nothing from universal-modder was installed, built or run. Paths starting `UM:` are relative to `~/DEV/git_repos/universal-modder`. `JAH:` is `ModularPlanters/.claude/skills/minecraft-modding`. `WF:` is `~/.claude/skills/neoforge-mod-workflow/SKILL.md`. `MCP:` is the installed package `@adhisang/minecraft-modding-mcp` 8.1.0 (the upstream README was fetched from the adhi-jp repo `main` branch).

## Recommendation

**Adopt parts, read-only. Do not install the plugin.** Keep the clone as a searchable reference, and use `rg` on `knowledge/` through the existing `referencing-local-repos` skill.

- It solves a different problem: modding finished PC games of any engine, driven through the running game, with generated art and a showcase video. NeoForge gets two lines of its Minecraft playbook (UM:`skills/mod-any-game/references/engines/minecraft.md:9-10`).
- It does not close the NeoForge lookup gap. It has no lookup tool, and its only pointer for this is the MCP you already run (UM:`skills/mod-any-game/references/engines/minecraft.md:21`).
- Its `mod-any-game` trigger overlaps `neoforge-mod-workflow`, and several of its rules contradict yours (see Q3).
- Installing it adds a fal MCP server that fails without `FAL_KEY` (UM:`CLAUDE.md:6-9`). `um win` refuses to run on macOS (UM:`um/win.py:45-47`).

Worth taking:

1. `knowledge/games/minecraft/neoforge-26-2-modpack-audit-perf-mods.md`, gotcha 19 (lines 198-211), lists 26.1 to 26.2 API changes. It is the most useful single item if this mod moves to 26.3 or a later 26.x. This is inference: the note covers 26.2 only and does not cover 26.3.
2. The same note, gotcha 21 (lines 216-220), describes a `javap -p` static check of mixin targets. It applies only if this mod adds mixins.
3. `skills/port-a-mod/SKILL.md`, read as a method document if a future mod port comes up.

The gap should be fixed in `neoforge-mod-workflow` instead (see Q4).

## Q1. What it is, who maintains it, maturity, install

- **What:** skills, a Python CLI (`um`), three subagents and a shared knowledge base of field notes for modding PC games (UM:`README.md:6-8`, `AGENTS.md:3-5`).
- **Maintainer:** Rehan, GitHub `rehan-remade` (UM:`plugin.json:6-9`). The most frequent author has 54 commits, followed by community contributors with 21 or fewer (`git shortlog -sn --all`).
- **Age:** 328 commits between 2026-09-29 and 2026-10-30, so about one month old (`git log`). Many recent commits are community `kb:` notes.
- **Version:** 0.2.0 (UM:`pyproject.toml:3`, `plugin.json:4`). SECURITY.md says there are no release branches and fixes land on `main` (UM:`SECURITY.md:8`).
- **License:** MIT (UM:`LICENSE:1-3`).
- **Tests:** 138 pytest functions across 11 files, counted with `rg -c`. They run in CI along with `um kb check --index` and `um publish check .` (UM:`.github/workflows/test.yml`). From the file names, they test the `um` CLI and its integrations. No test file is named for Minecraft. I did not run them.
- **Size:** 36M of files plus 41M of `.git`. Knowledge is 6.9M with 339 files. Examples are 19M.
- **Claude Code install:** `/plugin marketplace add rehan-remade/universal-modder`, then `/plugin install universal-modder@universal-modder` (UM:`README.md:35`). Skills are namespaced as `/universal-modder:mod-any-game` (UM:`CLAUDE.md:4`).

**README mismatch:** the README table lists 12 skills (UM:`README.md:136-147`), while `skills/` holds 13. `blitz3d-decomp` is missing from the table.

## Q2. Real loader and version support

There is no NeoForge-specific code. Support means prose guidance plus knowledge notes.

| Item | What the source shows | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Loader detection | Filename globs only: `*fabric-loader*`, `*neoforge*`, `*forge-*.jar` | UM:`um/scan.py:360` |
| Route hint | The string "Fabric (Mixin) or NeoForge", pointing at `minecraft.md` | UM:`um/scan.py:425` |
| Other NeoForge mentions outside knowledge, examples and docs | A `port-a-mod` description, one row in `publish-mod`, and the playbook | UM:`skills/port-a-mod/SKILL.md:3`, `skills/publish-mod/SKILL.md:28` |
| Playbook on NeoForge | Two lines: successor of Forge, MDK template, capabilities and events | UM:`skills/mod-any-game/references/engines/minecraft.md:9-10` |
| Knowledge notes naming NeoForge | Three indexed: 1.21.1 dimension, 1.21.1 GameTests, 26.2 modpack audit | UM:`knowledge/INDEX.md:131,138,310` |

**NeoForge 26.1.2 with Java 25 and unobfuscated names:**

- The skills do not state it. The playbook has no Java 25 line, and it frames mappings around Mojang's "obfuscation maps" and Loom's `genSources` (UM:`minecraft.md:14-15`). The reverse-engineering skill also says to use Loom `genSources` with Mojang mappings (UM:`skills/reverse-engineering/SKILL.md:36`). Neither applies to a ModDevGradle 26.x project.
- One community note gets it right for 26.2: NeoForge 26.2.0.88, FML 11.0.16, Java 25, unobfuscated (UM:`knowledge/games/minecraft/neoforge-26-2-modpack-audit-perf-mods.md:6,36-37`). That project built with plain `javac` and no Gradle (line 33), so it says nothing about ModDevGradle.
- No knowledge note targets NeoForge 26.1.x. The only 26.1 mentions are incidental (the same note, lines 90, 188, 198).
- The two `ModDevGradle` hits are both 1.21.1 notes.

Fabric gets noticeably more coverage, including a 26.x note (UM:`knowledge/techniques/fabric-mod-for-26-x-without-mappings.md`) and a 1.7.10 to 1.20.1 mapping table.

## Q3. Comparison

| Capability | universal-modder | `minecraft-modding` (Jahrome) | `neoforge-mod-workflow` | adhi-jp MCP |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Scope | Any PC game | NeoForge, Fabric, Forge, Architectury (JAH:`SKILL.md:12-17`) | NeoForge only (WF: Scope) | Minecraft Java, any loader |
| NeoForge 26.x guidance | None in skills; one 26.2 note | Labelled 26.x sections (JAH:`SKILL.md:22-28,226-232`) | Version table, 26.1 default | Unobfuscated 26.1+ handled (MCP README:309) |
| Code patterns and checklists | No | Yes (JAH:`SKILL.md:402-437`, `references/common-patterns.md`) | Defers to Jahrome | No |
| API lookup against the exact version | No | No | Sets the order, MCP first | Yes, 41 tools |
| Checkpoints that stop for approval | No; it runs a full 10-step loop | No | Yes | n/a |
| Verification | Running game as the oracle, screenshots, logs | Lists Gradle tasks | Repo recipes, GameTests, CI variants | Mixin, AW and AT validation |
| Prior art from other modders | Yes, the main asset | No | No | No |
| Asset generation | fal, ComfyUI, Sprixen, Voidless | No | No | No |
| Sprite and 3D to sprite pipeline | Yes | No | No | No |
| Game window automation | Windows and WSL only (UM:`um/win.py:45-47`) | No | Asks before `runClient` | No |
| Showcase video editing | Yes | No | No | No |
| Mod porting method | Yes (`port-a-mod`) | No | No | Version diffs |
| Release lint | `um publish check` | No | No | No |
| Build check script | No | `scripts/check-build.sh`, requires Java 25 on 26.x (JAH:`scripts/check-build.sh:78-82`) | No | No |

**Only universal-modder:** cross-game field notes, asset generation and the sprite pipeline, video editing, the porting method, the three-agent team.

**Only the current tools:** exact-version API lookups, access-transformer validation, approval checkpoints, the optional-dependency GameTest variants, 26.x code patterns.

**Overlap:** "how do I structure a Minecraft mod", where Jahrome is the stronger source for this version. `reverse-engineering` also overlaps the REA `reverse-engineer-anything` skill you already have.

**Conflicts if installed:**

| Topic | universal-modder says | Your setup says |
|---|---|---|
| Skill trigger | `mod-any-game`: use when the user wants to "mod, extend, hack on" a game (UM:`skills/mod-any-game/SKILL.md:3`) | `neoforge-mod-workflow`: use for any change to a NeoForge mod repo. Both can match a request to add a feature (inference). `WF` claims precedence over `minecraft-modding` only. |
| Commits | "Commit each working step" (UM:`skills/mod-any-game/SKILL.md:105-106`). "One commit per unit, pushed every session" (UM:`skills/port-a-mod/SKILL.md:217`) | Global `CLAUDE.md`: no commit or push unless told |
| Verification | "The running game is the oracle" (UM:`skills/mod-any-game/SKILL.md:118`). `runClient` is "the perfect agent oracle" (UM:`minecraft.md:7-8`) | Repo: `just check` and `just lint`. `WF`: ask before `runClient` |
| New files | `MODLOG.md` in the working folder (UM:`skills/mod-any-game/SKILL.md:52`) | "Don't add files when editing an existing one works". The repo is public and session logs are pushed. |
| Pacing | Takes the idea all the way to a recorded clip (UM:`skills/mod-any-game/SKILL.md:8-9`) | One slice, then stop and report |
| Publishing | `publish-mod` and `share-field-notes`; the latter triggers "at the end of any modding or reverse-engineering session" (UM:`skills/share-field-notes/SKILL.md:3`) | `just release-check` and `release.yml` publish this mod. PRs do need your approval on both sides (UM:`um/kb.py:14`). |
| AI disclosure | Disclose which agent and model built it (UM:`skills/publish-mod/SKILL.md:44-45`) | No AI attribution trailers in commits. The scope differs, but the release text is your call. |
| Mappings | Loom, `genSources`, obfuscation maps (UM:`minecraft.md:14-15`) | 26.x is unobfuscated; ModDevGradle (`WF`, `build.gradle:5`) |

Hooks do not conflict. The plugin registers only a `SessionStart` hook (UM:`hooks/hooks.json`), so it does not touch `enforce-tools.sh`.

## Q4. Does it solve the lookup gap?

**No.** A search of `knowledge/` and `skills/` finds no mention of `net.neoforged.fml`, `ModList.get` or `isLoaded`, and no mention of `ResourceHandler` or `EnergyHandler`. The only AE2 hit is a Fabric note saying no AE2 adapters were written (UM:`knowledge/games/minecraft/kindred-local-llm-ai-companion-fabric.md:170`).

**The gap is narrower than reported this session.** New test results against the existing MCP:

| Lookup | Target | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `EnergyHandler` source outline, `get-class-source` | `dependency`, explicit version `26.1.2.116`, with `projectPath` | **Works.** `origin: local-m2`, read from source |
| `EnergyHandler`, `find-class` | `dependency`, `versionFromProject: true` | **Fails.** `ERR_DEPENDENCY_VERSION_UNRESOLVED`: 16 cached NeoForge versions, refuses to pick |
| `loader` `ModList`, `find-class` | `dependency` on `net.neoforged.fancymodloader:loader`, `versionFromProject: true` | **Fails** the same way, with 8 cached versions |
| `ModList.isLoaded`, `get-class-members` | `jar`, `loader-11.0.15.jar` | **Works.** `public boolean isLoaded(java.lang.String)` |
| `appeng.api.networking.IGrid`, `find-class` | `jar`, `appliedenergistics2-26.1.13-beta.jar` | **Works** |

**So the earlier statement that "only a jar target works" was too strong.** A `dependency` target with an explicit version works for source lookups. `get-class-members` needs a binary, and that dependency artifact has none (the `ERR_CONTEXT_UNRESOLVED` from earlier), so it needs a `jar` target.

**Why `workspace` targets miss these classes.** `build/moddev/artifacts/` holds only `minecraft-patched-26.1.2.116*.jar`, and none of those jars contain `EnergyHandler` or `ModList` (checked with `unzip -l`). Even a correctly resolved loader-scope artifact would not contain them. The session's `workspace` errors also reported the same artifact id as the vanilla `version` lookup, so whether `loader` scope ever selected the patched jar here is not established.

**The FML version for this repo is 11.0.15**, from `neoforge-26.1.2.116.pom:74` in the Gradle cache. This settles what was left open earlier.

**Suggested change to `neoforge-mod-workflow`:**

| To read | Target |
|---|---|
| Vanilla | `{kind: version, value: <mc version>}` |
| NeoForge source | `{kind: dependency, group: net.neoforged, name: neoforge, version: <neo_version>}` |
| NeoForge members, or any source read that fails | `{kind: jar, value: <neoforge-<ver>-universal.jar>}` |
| FML (`ModList`) | `jar` target on `net.neoforged.fancymodloader:loader`, at the version in the NeoForge pom |
| AE2 and other addons | `jar` target on the jar in `~/.gradle/caches/modules-2` |

Avoid `versionFromProject` on this machine, because many versions are cached. The error's hint names `neoforge_version`, and this repo uses `neo_version`. Renaming a property in `gradle.properties` is not needed, because explicit versions work.

## Q5. What installing it does to the machine

| Effect | Detail | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Disk | Plugin copy of the repo, 36M of files. Location under `~/.claude/plugins/cache` is inferred from your other plugins. | `du`, inference |
| Skills and agents | 13 skills and 3 agents added to every session's listing where the plugin is enabled (inference). Agents set no `tools:` restriction in their frontmatter, so they get the default tool set. | UM:`agents/*.md:1-4` |
| Hook | `SessionStart` on startup, resume, clear and compact. Appends the plugin's `bin/` to `PATH` through `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE`. Nothing else. | UM:`hooks/hooks.json`, `hooks/add-to-path.sh:7-9` |
| MCP | `fal` over HTTP at `mcp.fal.ai`, with a `Bearer ${FAL_KEY}` header. With no key it sends the literal string, gets a 401 and does not fall back to OAuth, so it shows as a failed server. | UM:`.mcp.json`, `CLAUDE.md:6-9` |
| Permissions | The plugin files request none. | UM:`.claude/settings.json`, `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` |
| Telemetry | No hits for `telemetry`, `analytics`, `posthog`, `sentry` or `mixpanel` outside knowledge, examples and docs. This is a static text search. | `rg` |
| Python env | The first `um` call runs `uv run --project <plugin root>`, which creates a `.venv` there (Pillow, numpy, PyYAML). | UM:`bin/um:4-5,14-15`, `pyproject.toml` |
| Files in your home folder | `~/.universal-modder` is created by any command that asks for the data directory, and holds backups and downloaded tools. `um <service> key set` writes `~/.secrets/fal-key`, `sprixen-key` or `voidless-key`. | UM:`um/common.py:64-66`, `um/backup.py:8`, `um/fal.py:86`, `um/sprixen.py:47`, `um/voidless.py:57` |
| Network, only when invoked | `um fal`, `um sprixen`, `um voidless` call their paid APIs. `um kb sync` pulls from GitHub, and `um kb search` syncs only when no local `knowledge/` exists, which a plugin install has (inference from UM:`um/kb.py:49-57,93-101`). `um kb pr --yes` branches, commits, pushes to a fork and opens a PR. | UM:`um/kb.py:66-78,393-399` |
| Windows only | `um win` downloads ffmpeg from BtbN releases and checks its SHA-256. It refuses to run on macOS. | UM:`um/win.py:40-47,100-121` |

## Unverified

- The tests and CLI were not run, by the rules of this research, so their pass state and real behavior are read from source only.
- The plugin's exact install path, and whether the marketplace copy includes `.git`.
- How much the extra skill listings cost per session.
- Whether `mod-any-game` would actually fire over `neoforge-mod-workflow` in practice. The overlap comes from reading the descriptions.
- Whether the MCP reads `neo_version` from `gradle.properties`. A literal search of its `dist` found neither `neo_version` nor `neoforge_version`, while its error hint names the latter.
- The MCP's own network hosts and any telemetry. My search for telemetry words matched unrelated identifiers such as `sawClassEntry`, and the host listing was inconclusive. I saw it fetch Mojang's client jar from `piston-data.mojang.com`.
====
## Step 1 result (tooling walkthrough)

- The `minecraft-modding` MCP is connected with 41 tools. `bunx` is 1.4.4 and Node is 26.13.0.
- Vanilla lookups against 26.1.2 work. NeoForge, FML and AE2 lookups need the targets in the table below.
- `neoforge-mod-workflow` and the repo verification rules were compared. CI's GameTest matrix (none, `-PnoAe2`, `-PnoAppliedFlux`) matches `just check`.

| Verification | Running game as the oracle, screenshots, logs | Lists Gradle tasks | Repo recipes, GameTests, CI variants | Mixin, AW and AT validation |
| Prior art from other modders | Yes, the main asset | No | No | No |
| Asset generation | fal, ComfyUI, Sprixen, Voidless | No | No | No |
| Sprite and 3D to sprite pipeline | Yes | No | No | No |
| Game window automation | Windows and WSL only (UM:`um/win.py:45-47`) | No | Asks before `runClient` | No |
| Showcase video editing | Yes | No | No | No |
| Mod porting method | Yes (`port-a-mod`) | No | No | Version diffs |
| Release lint | `um publish check` | No | No | No |
| Build check script | No | `scripts/check-build.sh`, requires Java 25 on 26.x (JAH:`scripts/check-build.sh:78-82`) | No | No |

**Only the current tools:** exact-version API lookups, access-transformer validation, approval checkpoints, the optional-dependency GameTest variants, 26.x code patterns.

**Overlap:** "how do I structure a Minecraft mod", where Jahrome is the stronger source for this version. `reverse-engineering` also overlaps the REA `reverse-engineer-anything` skill you already have.

Hooks do not conflict. The plugin registers only a `SessionStart` hook (UM:`hooks/hooks.json`), so it does not touch `enforce-tools.sh`.

## Q4. Does it solve the lookup gap?

**No.** A search of `knowledge/` and `skills/` finds no mention of `net.neoforged.fml`, `ModList.get` or `isLoaded`, and no mention of `ResourceHandler` or `EnergyHandler`. The only AE2 hit is a Fabric note saying no AE2 adapters were written (UM:`knowledge/games/minecraft/kindred-local-llm-ai-companion-fabric.md:170`).

**The gap is narrower than reported this session.** New test results against the existing MCP:

| Lookup | Target | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `EnergyHandler` source outline, `get-class-source` | `dependency`, explicit version `26.1.2.116`, with `projectPath` | **Works.** `origin: local-m2`, read from source |
| `EnergyHandler`, `find-class` | `dependency`, `versionFromProject: true` | **Fails.** `ERR_DEPENDENCY_VERSION_UNRESOLVED`: 16 cached NeoForge versions, refuses to pick |
| `loader` `ModList`, `find-class` | `dependency` on `net.neoforged.fancymodloader:loader`, `versionFromProject: true` | **Fails** the same way, with 8 cached versions |
| `ModList.isLoaded`, `get-class-members` | `jar`, `loader-11.0.15.jar` | **Works.** `public boolean isLoaded(java.lang.String)` |
| `appeng.api.networking.IGrid`, `find-class` | `jar`, `appliedenergistics2-26.1.13-beta.jar` | **Works** |

**So the earlier statement that "only a jar target works" was too strong.** A `dependency` target with an explicit version works for source lookups. `get-class-members` needs a binary, and that dependency artifact has none (the `ERR_CONTEXT_UNRESOLVED` from earlier), so it needs a `jar` target.

**Why `workspace` targets miss these classes.** `build/moddev/artifacts/` holds only `minecraft-patched-26.1.2.116*.jar`, and none of those jars contain `EnergyHandler` or `ModList` (checked with `unzip -l`). Even a correctly resolved loader-scope artifact would not contain them. The session's `workspace` errors also reported the same artifact id as the vanilla `version` lookup, so whether `loader` scope ever selected the patched jar here is not established.

**The FML version for this repo is 11.0.15**, from `neoforge-26.1.2.116.pom:74` in the Gradle cache. This settles what was left open earlier.

**Suggested change to `neoforge-mod-workflow`:**

| To read | Target |
|---|---|
| Vanilla | `{kind: version, value: <mc version>}` |
| NeoForge source | `{kind: dependency, group: net.neoforged, name: neoforge, version: <neo_version>}` |
| NeoForge members, or any source read that fails | `{kind: jar, value: <neoforge-<ver>-universal.jar>}` |
| FML (`ModList`) | `jar` target on `net.neoforged.fancymodloader:loader`, at the version in the NeoForge pom |
| AE2 and other addons | `jar` target on the jar in `~/.gradle/caches/modules-2` |

Avoid `versionFromProject` on this machine, because many versions are cached. The error's hint names `neoforge_version`, and this repo uses `neo_version`. Renaming a property in `gradle.properties` is not needed, because explicit versions work.

## Q5. What installing it does to the machine

| Effect | Detail | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Disk | Plugin copy of the repo, 36M of files. Location under `~/.claude/plugins/cache` is inferred from your other plugins. | `du`, inference |
| Skills and agents | 13 skills and 3 agents added to every session's listing where the plugin is enabled (inference). Agents set no `tools:` restriction in their frontmatter, so they get the default tool set. | UM:`agents/*.md:1-4` |
| Hook | `SessionStart` on startup, resume, clear and compact. Appends the plugin's `bin/` to `PATH` through `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE`. Nothing else. | UM:`hooks/hooks.json`, `hooks/add-to-path.sh:7-9` |
| MCP | `fal` over HTTP at `mcp.fal.ai`, with a `Bearer ${FAL_KEY}` header. With no key it sends the literal string, gets a 401 and does not fall back to OAuth, so it shows as a failed server. | UM:`.mcp.json`, `CLAUDE.md:6-9` |
| Permissions | The plugin files request none. | UM:`.claude/settings.json`, `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` |
| Telemetry | No hits for `telemetry`, `analytics`, `posthog`, `sentry` or `mixpanel` outside knowledge, examples and docs. This is a static text search. | `rg` |
| Python env | The first `um` call runs `uv run --project <plugin root>`, which creates a `.venv` there (Pillow, numpy, PyYAML). | UM:`bin/um:4-5,14-15`, `pyproject.toml` |
| Files in your home folder | `~/.universal-modder` is created by any command that asks for the data directory, and holds backups and downloaded tools. `um <service> key set` writes `~/.secrets/fal-key`, `sprixen-key` or `voidless-key`. | UM:`um/common.py:64-66`, `um/backup.py:8`, `um/fal.py:86`, `um/sprixen.py:47`, `um/voidless.py:57` |
| Network, only when invoked | `um fal`, `um sprixen`, `um voidless` call their paid APIs. `um kb sync` pulls from GitHub, and `um kb search` syncs only when no local `knowledge/` exists, which a plugin install has (inference from UM:`um/kb.py:49-57,93-101`). `um kb pr --yes` branches, commits, pushes to a fork and opens a PR. | UM:`um/kb.py:66-78,393-399` |
| Windows only | `um win` downloads ffmpeg from BtbN releases and checks its SHA-256. It refuses to run on macOS. | UM:`um/win.py:40-47,100-121` |

## Unverified

- The tests and CLI were not run, by the rules of this research, so their pass state and real behavior are read from source only.
- The plugin's exact install path, and whether the marketplace copy includes `.git`.
- How much the extra skill listings cost per session.
- Whether `mod-any-game` would actually fire over `neoforge-mod-workflow` in practice. The overlap comes from reading the descriptions.

- The MCP's own network hosts and any telemetry. My search for telemetry words matched unrelated identifiers such as `sawClassEntry`, and the host listing was inconclusive. I saw it fetch Mojang's client jar from `piston-data.mojang.com`.

---
name: neoforge-mod-workflow
description: Julian's rules for working on NeoForge Minecraft mods (26.1, 26.3 or 1.21.1). Use for any change to a NeoForge mod repo, such as adding a block, item, entity, machine, recipe, config, networking or GameTest, and when starting a new mod from an empty folder. Sets the supported versions, where to look up APIs, the checkpoint workflow that stops for approval, and how to verify. Use together with the minecraft-modding skill, which holds the code patterns.
---

# NeoForge mod workflow

These rules sit on top of the `minecraft-modding` skill. That skill has the code patterns; this one decides versions, lookups, pacing and verification. Where they disagree, this one wins.

## Scope

- NeoForge only. If a request needs Fabric, Forge or a multiloader setup, say so and stop.
- Supported Minecraft versions:

| Version | Java | Mappings | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 26.1 (default for new mods) | 25 | None. 26.x is unobfuscated and uses official names. | Start from the current NeoForge generator or MDK for that exact version. |
| 26.3 | 25 | None. | Same as 26.1. Check the NeoForge changelog for API changes since 26.1. |
| 1.21.1 | 21 | Mojang mappings plus Parchment. | NeoForge 21.1.x. Classes use `ResourceLocation`, not `Identifier`. |

- In an existing repo, the version is whatever `gradle.properties` says. Never change it, or any dependency version, unless asked.

## Looking things up

Never write an API name, method signature, registry name, event name or version number from memory. Check it first, in this order:

1. The `minecraft-modding` MCP server (adhi-jp), against the project's exact Minecraft version: `check-symbol-exists` or `batch-symbol-exists` before using a class or method, `get-class-source` and `get-class-members` to read vanilla code, `get-registry-data` for registry ids, `validate-access-transformer` after editing an access transformer, and `analyze-mod-jar` or `search-mod-source` for a dependency's API.
   The `target` decides whether a class is found. NeoForge and FML classes are not in the vanilla artifact, and `workspace` targets did not find them either, because the patched jars in `build/moddev/artifacts` do not contain them.

   | To read | Target |
   |---|---|
   | Vanilla | `{kind: version, value: <mc version>}` |
   | NeoForge source | `{kind: dependency, group: net.neoforged, name: neoforge, version: <neo version>}` |
   | NeoForge members, or any source read that fails | `{kind: jar, value: <path to neoforge-<version>-universal.jar>}`, found under `~/.gradle/caches/modules-2` |
   | FML, such as `ModList` | `jar` target on `net.neoforged.fancymodloader:loader`, at the version in the NeoForge pom |
   | AE2 and other addons | `jar` target on the addon's jar under `~/.gradle/caches/modules-2` |

   Pass explicit versions. `versionFromProject` fails with `ERR_DEPENDENCY_VERSION_UNRESOLVED` when several versions of the artifact are cached.
2. The NeoForge docs at `https://docs.neoforged.net` with the matching version selected, and the NeoForge changelog for that version.
3. Local clones under `~/DEV/git_repos` (see the `referencing-local-repos` skill), especially for addon APIs such as AE2.
4. The `minecraft-modding` skill's examples. Its `references/neoforge-api.md` is for 1.21.x only; for 26.x, use the sections labelled 26.x in `references/common-patterns.md`.

If a lookup fails and the answer still matters, say what could not be verified instead of guessing.

## Checkpoints

Work in small slices and stop at each checkpoint. Do not chain slices together without approval.

1. **Orient.** Read `gradle.properties`, the build script, `neoforge.mods.toml`, and the repo's `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `DEVELOPMENT.md` and `justfile` if present. Follow the repo's own conventions over this skill's.
2. **Plan, then stop.** Before writing code, give a short plan: what changes, which files, which existing classes are reused, how it will be verified, and any open question. Wait for approval.
3. **Implement one slice.** One feature or one coherent part of a feature, never the whole backlog.
4. **Verify the slice** (see below), then **stop and report**: what changed, what was verified and how, and what was not verified. Propose the next slice instead of starting it.

Always ask before:

- adding, removing or upgrading a dependency, or editing `build.gradle`, `settings.gradle` or `gradle.properties`;
- deleting or renaming files, registry ids or config keys, because renames break existing worlds and configs;
- changing saved-data, attachment or data-component formats that existing worlds already contain;
- running `runClient` or `runServer`, which open long-running processes;
- anything the plan did not cover.

## Verification

Use the repo's `justfile` recipes when they exist; otherwise call Gradle directly.

| After | Run |
|---|---|
| Any Java change | `./gradlew build` (compiles and runs unit tests) |
| Gameplay logic: blocks, machines, recipes, entities, persistence | `./gradlew runGameTestServer`, plus each variant the repo's CI runs (for example optional-dependency flags) |
| Datagen providers changed | The repo's datagen task (`runData` or `runClientData`), then inspect the diff in the generated resources |
| Access transformer changed | `validate-access-transformer` through the MCP server, then a build |

Run these once at the end of a slice, not after every edit. Hot reload is usually already running, so do not rebuild between edits unless asked. Where the repo has `just check` and `just lint`, those replace the build and GameTest rows (`just check` does not build the jar; CI does).

Report failures with the actual error output. A slice that adds gameplay logic without a GameTest needs a stated reason.

Rules that apply to every slice:

- Server-authoritative logic. Validate every client packet.
- Client-only classes live in client packages and never load on a dedicated server.
- Every registered block or item gets its model, texture, language entry, loot table or recipe in the same slice. No missing textures or raw translation keys.
- Item state uses data components; world and entity state uses saved data or data attachments.

## Starting a new mod

For a new mod from an empty folder, copy `references/new-mod-prompt.md` (next to this file) into the new folder as `PROMPT.md`. Fill in its placeholders with the user rather than inventing them. The checkpoints above still apply: the design bible is the first checkpoint, then each MVP slice.

Reference for writing any document an agent consumes: a skill, an `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md`, a doc reached by a pointer. The packaging differs; the writing does not: the same levers make each one predictable, since the agent takes the same _process_ every run rather than producing the same output.

When the document you're writing is a skill, read [`SKILL-MECHANICS.md`](SKILL-MECHANICS.md) for frontmatter, invocation choice, and router skills.

## Context pointers

A **context pointer** is a reference held in the agent's context that names some out-of-context material and encodes the condition for reaching it. A skill's description is one; a line in `AGENTS.md` naming a doc is the same object. The pointer's _wording_, not its target, decides when the agent reaches the material, and how reliably. A must-have target behind a weakly worded pointer is a variance bug: sharpen the wording first, and inline the material only if sharpening fails.

A pointer does two jobs: state what the material is, and list the **branches** that should trigger reaching it (a branch is a distinct case the document handles, so different runs take different paths through it). Every word of an always-loaded pointer costs on every turn, so it earns even harder pruning than the body:

- **Front-load the leading word**: the pointer is where it does its triggering work.

**Co-location** is the within-file companion: where the ladder decides _how far down_ a piece sits, co-location decides _what sits beside it_ once there. **Sprawl** is the failure mode here: a document simply too long, even when every line is live and unique. Attention thins across the excess, and every extra line is one more to keep relevant. Every step ends on a **completion criterion**, the condition that tells the agent the work is done. Two properties make it a lever:

# Modular Planters

NeoForge 26.1.2 addon for Agritech: Evolved (ATE) that merges many planters into one multiblock. DEVELOPMENT.md has the commands, layout, dev mods and release steps. CONTRIBUTING.md has the pull request rules.

The repo is public, and each push also sends Entire session logs to `origin`, so keep private paths and personal details out of commits.

## Every task

- Run `just check` and `just lint` to verify a change.
- The mod must load with any optional mod missing.
- Keep save keys and registry ids as they are, because renaming breaks existing worlds. The save key `soil_and_modules` keeps its old name, and ATE's own names stay as ATE has them.
- Keep merged history as it is, because `.git-blame-ignore-revs` names the reformat commit e1a9a58, and a squash or rebase breaks that.
- Player-facing text uses the block names from `en_us.json`, "upgrades" instead of "modules", and "Advanced Planter" instead of "Powered Planter".

## Read the doc that matches the task

- [GLOSSARY.md](GLOSSARY.md): before naming anything in code, docs or questions. [docs/adr/](docs/adr/) holds the decisions that are hard to reverse.
- [Verifying changes](docs/agents/verifying.md): before running datagen, or when a change touches Jade or the Oracle Index book.
- [Optional mods and the ME link](docs/agents/optional-mods.md): before touching `ae2` code, `mod_loaded` conditions or `MeLink`.
- [GameTests](docs/agents/gametests.md): before writing or debugging a GameTest.
- [Docs, wiki and store pages](docs/agents/docs-and-wiki.md): before editing `wiki/` or `docs/description.md`.
- [Build and tooling](docs/agents/build-and-tooling.md): before changing CI, hooks or the Gradle setup, or before using `entire graph` for a refactor.

## Agent skills

### Issue tracker

Issues live in GitHub Issues for julian-perge/ModularPlanters, through the `gh` CLI. See `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.

### Triage labels

The five default labels: needs-triage, needs-info, ready-for-agent, ready-for-human, wontfix. See `docs/agents/triage-labels.md`.

### Domain docs

Single-context: one `GLOSSARY.md` and `docs/adr/` at the repo root. See `docs/agents/domain.md`.

@.entire/agent-guide.md
# Modular Planters

NeoForge 26.1.2 addon for Agritech: Evolved (ATE) that merges many planters into one multiblock. DEVELOPMENT.md has the commands, layout, dev mods and release steps. CONTRIBUTING.md has the pull request rules.

The repo is public, and each push also sends Entire session logs to `origin`, so keep private paths and personal details out of commits.

## Every task

- Run `just check` and `just lint` to verify a change.
- The mod must load with any optional mod missing.
- Keep save keys and registry ids as they are, because renaming breaks existing worlds. The save key `soil_and_modules` keeps its old name, and ATE's own names stay as ATE has them.
- Keep merged history as it is, because `.git-blame-ignore-revs` names the reformat commit e1a9a58, and a squash or rebase breaks that.
- Player-facing text uses the block names from `en_us.json`, "upgrades" instead of "modules", and "Advanced Planter" instead of "Powered Planter".

- [GLOSSARY.md](GLOSSARY.md): before naming anything in code, docs or questions. [docs/adr/](docs/adr/) holds the decisions that are hard to reverse.
